```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

library(targets)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(gt)
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(hmmTMB))

## Handle both pipeline rendering (from project root) and standalone rendering
## (from inside quarto_reports/), same convention as covariate_summary.qmd.
store_path <- if (dir.exists("_targets")) "_targets" else "../_targets"
r_path     <- if (dir.exists("_targets")) "r" else "../r"

## season_info() (r/a_season_info.R) -- used below (forecast-period) to label which season the
## risk map's own covariate period falls in and which season it therefore forecasts. Sourced
## directly (not tar_load()'d, a plain function not a target), same pattern as covariate_summary.qmd.
source(file.path(r_path, "a_season_info.R"))
## hindcast_auc() (r/d_score_plague_hindcast.R) -- used below (mutze-1984) for the cell-level AUC.
source(file.path(r_path, "d_score_plague_hindcast.R"))

tar_load(
  c(
    fit_zones_sf, aus_shp, grdc_subregion_adj,
    hmm_data, plague_hmm, plague_hmm_unsupervised, plague_hmm_ppc, plague_hmm_pseudores,
    plague_risk_map_supervised, plague_risk_map_unsupervised,
    plague_risk_map_uncertainty_supervised, plague_risk_map_uncertainty_unsupervised,
    plague_risk_map_nowcast_supervised, plague_risk_map_nowcast_unsupervised,
    survey_state_wide, yearly_plague_occurrence, recent_plague_maps,
    rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak, gpp_rolling_raster_6, soil_moisture_raster_coarse, min_temp_raster_coarse,
    gpp_rolling_raster_6_nowcast, soil_moisture_raster_coarse_nowcast,
    plague_hindcast_supervised, plague_hindcast_unsupervised,
    plague_hindcast_scores_supervised, plague_hindcast_scores_unsupervised, mutze_plague_maps
  ),
  store = store_path
)

## Supervised vs. unsupervised is a STANDING comparison throughout this report (2026-08), not a
## one-off toggle -- both models are always fit (Section D, _targets.R), and every prediction-side
## target (plague_risk_map_*, plague_risk_map_uncertainty_*) is built for both via a tar_map() over
## model variant (_targets.R), the same "same computation, several variants" pattern this pipeline
## already uses for GPP/rain rolling windows. This list is the single place that defines which
## models are compared and how they're labelled -- every section below (coefficient tables, risk
## maps, uncertainty maps) loops over this rather than hard-coding "plague_hmm" -- so a third model
## variant later (e.g. a re-anchored version) needs one more entry here (plus its own tar_map() row
## in _targets.R) rather than a hand-copied section.
## risk_map_nowcast added alongside risk_map (2026-09) -- same fitted model, same predict_plague_risk()
## call, just fed gpp_rolling_raster_6_nowcast/soil_moisture_raster_coarse_nowcast in place of their
## season-end-trimmed namesakes (_targets.R), so it lands on the latest complete calendar month
## instead of waiting for the next Feb/May/Aug/Nov boundary. No uncertainty variant yet (deliberately
## deferred, see _targets.R's own TO-DO note and r/d_predict_plague_risk.R's header) -- so
## risk_map_uncertainty stays keyed to the season-end-aligned model only.
model_variants <- list(
  Supervised   = list(hmm = plague_hmm,              risk_map = plague_risk_map_supervised,   risk_map_uncertainty = plague_risk_map_uncertainty_supervised,   risk_map_nowcast = plague_risk_map_nowcast_supervised),
  Unsupervised = list(hmm = plague_hmm_unsupervised, risk_map = plague_risk_map_unsupervised, risk_map_uncertainty = plague_risk_map_uncertainty_unsupervised, risk_map_nowcast = plague_risk_map_nowcast_unsupervised)
)

## Same hazard palette as the standalone risk-map artifact this report
## supersedes as the pipeline's own copy -- muted sage (calm) through ochre
## to brick red (severe), not a default viridis/RdYlGn scale, so any output
## showing plague_risk reads consistently across the project.
hazard_colors <- c("#3F5B45", "#7C8C43", "#C99A34", "#BE5F2C", "#7A2626")

## Shared national outline (WGS84) -- used as spatial context by both fig-spatial-key-years and
## fig-risk-map below, built once here rather than duplicated in each chunk.
aus_sf <- st_as_sf(aus_shp) |> st_transform(4326)

## The 4 chewcard streams (chewcard_count = cards 1-10, chewcard_block2/3/4 = cards 11-20/21-30/
## 31-40, r/d_fit_plague_hmm.R) share every coefficient by construction (tied across blocks) -- so
## anywhere a diagnostic would just repeat the same fitted values 4 times, chewcard_count alone
## stands in for all four; pseudo-residuals are the one exception, since they're computed against
## each block's own distinct rows.
chewcard_streams <- c("chewcard_count", "chewcard_block2", "chewcard_block3", "chewcard_block4")

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
)
```

## Overview

Section D fits a two-state (not-plague / plague) hidden Markov model (`hmmTMB`) to the seasonal survey panel Section C builds, then applies the fitted model to the gridded covariate surface to produce a continuous plague-risk map. This report is the empirical companion to `r/d_fit_plague_hmm.R` -- that file's own header carries the full design rationale and investigation history (why a semi-supervised HMM, every covariate/family/anchoring choice tried and why it was adopted or reverted); this page shows the numbers themselves, generated live from the pipeline's own targets so it can't silently drift out of sync with the model actually in use.

Two versions of the same specification are fit, and compared throughout this report as a standing design, not a one-off check: **`plague_hmm`** (labelled **Supervised** below), the real semi-supervised model (known plague occurrences anchor the hidden state where available -- see [Data and anchoring]), and **`plague_hmm_unsupervised`** (labelled **Unsupervised**), identical in every other respect but with every anchor wiped to `NA`, so the HMM discovers its own 2-state split purely from the observation/transition data. The gap between the two (see [Validation against known history]) is a direct measure of how much the anchors themselves are doing -- worth watching in its own right whenever the anchoring pipeline's own upstream data is mid-update, since the unsupervised model's own numbers don't move when only the anchors' inputs have changed. Every prediction-side output (risk map, its own uncertainty) is built for both models (`_targets.R`'s own `tar_map()` over model variant), not just one -- see `model_variants` above.

## Data and anchoring

```{r}
#| label: tbl-zones

## Derived live from hmm_data's own states, not a hand-maintained list (hmm_states, _targets.R) --
## WA joined 2026-09 once the transition formula's own zone slope moved to a hierarchical spec (see
## [Zone-specific deviations]), so this table (and its own title below) tracks that automatically.
fit_states <- sort(unique(hmm_data$aus_state))

tibble::tibble(
  State = fit_states,
  Paddocks = sapply(fit_states, function(s) n_distinct(hmm_data$ID[hmm_data$aus_state == s]))
) |>
  arrange(desc(Paddocks)) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = sprintf("The %d states the model is fit to", length(fit_states)))
```

The model pools every paddock across these `r length(fit_states)` states into one fit -- a single-zone fit was tried and found non-viable (see `r/d_fit_plague_hmm.R`), since one zone's own anchor data gave the model no examples of ever leaving the plague state. One zone, `"Qld Central"`, is excluded entirely: its 17 paddocks have zero plague anchors and zero real observations of any kind since 2008, and including it produced the same degenerate-fit signature documented for other thin-data cases elsewhere (`r/d_fit_plague_hmm.R`). WA joined the fit 2026-09, once the transition formula's own zone-varying `rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak` slope moved to a hierarchical (partially-pooled) spec -- see [Zone-specific deviations] -- WA's own 4 zones weren't viable under the earlier fixed-interaction spec, for the same "one zone with no examples of leaving plague" identifiability reason. `r n_distinct(hmm_data$ID)` paddocks remain across `r n_distinct(hmm_data$ae_zone)` zones.

```{r}
#| label: anchor-counts

n_plague    <- sum(hmm_data$state == 2, na.rm = TRUE)
n_nonplague <- sum(hmm_data$state == 1, na.rm = TRUE)
n_both <- hmm_data |>
  filter(!is.na(state)) |>
  group_by(ID) |>
  summarise(has_2 = any(state == 2), has_1 = any(state == 1), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(has_2, has_1) |>
  nrow()

## anchor_plague_state() (r/c_anchor_plague_state.R) anchors from recent_plague_maps -- hand-
## digitised, paddock-scale plague-extent polygons, one gpkg per season (r/c_read_recent_plague_
## maps.R) -- REPLACING (2026-09) the earlier state x year / state x season (a)+(b) rule (still
## available in r_not_in_use/c_anchor_plague_state.R, for the full history of that rule's own
## development). A paddock-season anchors plague_state = 2 if its own location falls inside any
## polygon mapped for that exact season (any severity), plague_state = 1 if it's outside every
## polygon mapped for a season recent_plague_maps DOES cover, and NA (unanchored) everywhere else --
## except that same paddock's own 2 seasons immediately before a plague_state = 2 anchor, where a
## forced plague_state = 1 is loosened back to NA (added 2026-09: a real outbreak is rarely
## confirmed the very first season it begins, so those lead-up seasons aren't confidently non-plague
## either).
mapped_years      <- sort(unique(recent_plague_maps$year))
first_mapped_year <- min(mapped_years)
n_pre_coverage_anchored <- hmm_data |>
  filter(year_adj < first_mapped_year, !is.na(state)) |>
  nrow()
```

Of `r nrow(hmm_data)` paddock-seasons, `r n_plague` are anchored to the plague state and `r n_nonplague` to the non-plague state (`r round(100*(n_plague+n_nonplague)/nrow(hmm_data), 1)`% of the panel), all of them within recent_plague_maps' own `r length(mapped_years)` mapped seasons (`r paste(mapped_years, collapse = ", ")`) (`r n_pre_coverage_anchored` rows anchored outside that coverage, confirming the rule really does leave every other season untouched). `r n_both` paddocks have both a plague and a non-plague anchor at different times, giving the model genuine before/after evidence of the transition it's meant to estimate.

```{r}
#| label: trigger-episodes

## Unlike the superseded (a)+(b) rule, this anchor has no persistence propagation -- every
## plague_state=2 row is its own independent point-in-polygon match, not a trigger multiplied
## forward across seasons -- so the anchored-row count above already IS the independent-event
## count. Broken down per mapped season here rather than recomputed.
anchors_by_season <- hmm_data |>
  filter(!is.na(state)) |>
  count(year_adj, state)
```

**Every one of the `r n_plague` plague-anchored rows above is a genuinely independent event** -- a paddock's own location falling inside a mapped polygon for that exact season, with no propagation to inflate the count -- spread across `r length(mapped_years)` mapped seasons (`r paste(mapped_years, collapse = ", ")`). **The transition coefficient this whole forecasting use case leans on is therefore estimated from exactly `r n_plague` independent events** -- a real small-N caveat worth keeping visible alongside the coefficient's own point estimate below, and a smaller number than the superseded rule's own (that rule's much broader 2013+ coverage came at the cost of state/subregion-grain, not paddock-grain, evidence).

`recent_plague_maps` has no coverage at all before `r first_mapped_year`, so the historic panel back to 1985 (`trap_count` only) is fully unanchored -- see `r/c_anchor_plague_state.R`'s header for why no fallback rule covers that stretch (the superseded (a)+(b) rule's own two attempts at one were tried and reverted; this rule doesn't reattempt them). Historic `trap_count` data still informs that stream's own distribution, but contributes no state-anchor evidence in either direction.

### Anchored states vs. the model's own estimate, by state

```{r}
#| label: fig-anchor-vs-model
#| fig-cap: "Anchored plague-state evidence fed into the fit (points, only where at least one paddock in that state-season has an anchor -- none before 2014) against the model's own smoothed Pr(plague state) (line, averaged across every paddock in that state-season) -- hmmTMB's state_probs(), not a hard Viterbi decode. Faceted by state to match the grain plague_state is itself anchored at."
#| fig-asp: 0.5

## state_probs() returns one row per hmm_data row, in the same order (confirmed live: at anchored
## rows, state_probs()'s own smoothed probability for the anchored state is exactly 1 -- hmmTMB
## fixes known states during estimation, so this isn't a coincidence, it's the alignment check).
state2_prob <- plague_hmm$state_probs()[, "state2"]
state2_prob_unsup <- plague_hmm_unsupervised$state_probs()[, "state2"]

## Row-level Viterbi agreement between the anchored and unsupervised models -- computed live so
## the prose number below can't drift out of sync with whichever model this chunk compares.
row_agreement <- round(100 * mean(plague_hmm$viterbi() == plague_hmm_unsupervised$viterbi()), 1)

## Same season_mid_month convention as raster_layer_dates() (r/b_raster_mean_series.R) -- the 15th
## of that season's own mid-month, purely for a continuous, sortable x-axis.
season_mid_month <- c(Summer = 1L, Autumn = 4L, Winter = 7L, Spring = 10L)

anchor_vs_model <- hmm_data |>
  mutate(
    state2_prob_model = state2_prob,
    state2_prob_unsup_model = state2_prob_unsup,
    anchored_plague    = dplyr::case_when(state == 2 ~ 1, state == 1 ~ 0, TRUE ~ NA_real_),
    season_str  = as.character(season_year_adj),
    season_name = sub("-.*", "", season_str),
    year_adj    = as.integer(sub(".*-", "", season_str)),
    date        = as.Date(paste(year_adj, season_mid_month[season_name], "15", sep = "-"))
  ) |>
  group_by(aus_state, date) |>
  summarise(
    anchored_frac = mean(anchored_plague, na.rm = TRUE),
    model_prob    = mean(state2_prob_model),
    model_prob_unsup = mean(state2_prob_unsup_model),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(anchor_vs_model, aes(date)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = model_prob, colour = "Anchored model (state_probs)"), linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(aes(y = model_prob_unsup, colour = "Unsupervised model (state_probs)"), linewidth = 0.4, linetype = "22") +
  geom_point(aes(y = anchored_frac, colour = "Anchored (ground truth)"), size = 1.2, na.rm = TRUE) +
  facet_wrap(~aus_state, ncol = 2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(
    `Anchored model (state_probs)`      = "#2166ac",
    `Unsupervised model (state_probs)`  = "#8c8c8c",
    `Anchored (ground truth)`           = hazard_colors[5]
  ), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Pr(plague state)") +
  theme(legend.position = "top", strip.text = element_text(size = 8.5))
```

Where anchor points sit near 0 or 1 and the anchored line tracks them closely, the fit is doing what it should. Divergence is the more informative case -- either the model finding independent support for a state the anchors don't confirm, or a sign the covariate relationship isn't transferring cleanly. The grey (unsupervised) line tracks the blue (anchored) one closely almost everywhere -- `r row_agreement`% row-level Viterbi agreement between the two. Divergence concentrated around recent_plague_maps' own mapped seasons (`r paste(mapped_years, collapse = ", ")`) would be the expected signature of the anchors doing real work, exactly what they're *for*: sharpening the estimate where independent regional evidence exists and the observation data alone wouldn't quite have been enough; sustained divergence elsewhere would be worth a closer look.

```{=html}
  <circle cx="98" cy="562" r="7" fill="#3F5B45" fill-opacity="0.4" stroke="#3F5B45" />
  <text x="112" y="566" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">S1 = not-plague</text>
  <circle cx="98" cy="582" r="7" fill="#7A2626" fill-opacity="0.4" stroke="#7A2626" />
  <text x="112" y="586" font-size="11" fill="currentColor">S2 = plague</text>
  <text x="270" y="562" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" opacity="0.75">Both streams and states repeat every season -- one HMM fit</text>
  <text x="270" y="578" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" opacity="0.75">per paddock, most paddock-seasons observe only 1-2 of the 3 streams.</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>The hidden not-plague/plague state forms a Markov chain across seasons (top): which of the four transition arrows applies each season is set by the process-model covariates in the box, not fixed. Whichever state a paddock is in that season (bottom) independently generates up to three response types, each with its own distribution family and detection-side covariates -- "tied" means that covariate's effect is constrained to be identical across states (or, for chewcard's extra blocks, across blocks too), on the view that it's a detection mechanism rather than a real state-dependent one, see [Fit diagnostics]. Semi-supervised anchoring is not shown here, see <a href="#data-and-anchoring">Data and anchoring</a>.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-spec

tibble::tribble(
  ~Component, ~Specification,
  "States", "2 (not-plague, plague)",
  "Transition formula", "~ rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak + s(ae_zone, by = rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak, bs = 're') + gpp_rolling6 + soil_moisture + min_temp + s(ae_zone, bs = 're'). rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak's own zone slope is a hierarchical (partially-pooled) random slope, not a fixed per-zone interaction -- see [Zone-specific deviations]. Structurally one-season-ahead only -- see [Prediction: current risk map]",
  "Initial state distribution", "stationary (not hmmTMB's own default of one estimated distribution per paddock -- too many free parameters relative to the anchor data available)",
  "trap_count", "Total captures per session (trap success; recaptures included). nbinom2 (mean/shape); mean ~season (tied across states) + a search-effort offset (log_trap_effort, coefficient fixed at 1, correcting for true trap-nights, 4-827, ~200x range). No ae_zone, crop/soil or shape formula -- see [Fit diagnostics] for why.",
  "burrow_count", "nbinom2 (mean/shape); mean ~season (tied) + ae_zone (free per state) + season:summer_zone_ne (tied) + gpp_finescale (tied) + crop group, crop stage and soil type (tied; missing crop as 'not recorded') + a search-effort offset (log_burrow_metres_searched, fixed at 1, correcting for burrow_transects_surveyed's own real variation).",
  "chewcard_count + 3 blocks", "betabinom (beta-binomial: prob = mean, sigma = overdispersion), trials fixed at 10 each. chewcard_count = cards 1-10; chewcard_block2/3/4 = cards 11-20/21-30/31-40 (r/a_data_rapid_session_summary.R), NA wherever that block wasn't deployed. prob ~season (tied) + crop group, crop stage and soil type (tied) + ae_zone (free per state); every coefficient additionally tied ACROSS the 4 blocks, since they measure the same underlying detection rate over however many transects were actually deployed. sigma ~1, free per state, tied across the 4 blocks."
) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
  gt::cols_width(Component ~ px(200))
```

"Tied" (season on all streams; crop group, crop stage and soil type on `burrow_count` and the chewcard streams; `gpp_finescale`/`season:summer_zone_ne` on `burrow_count`; and everything across the 4 chewcard blocks) means hmmTMB's own coefficient is constrained to one shared, freely-estimated value via its `fixpar` "estimate to a common value" mechanism, not independently fit per state/stream -- chosen on the view that these are detection mechanisms (ground-cover/crop-stage visibility, or just more replicates of the same card-reading process), which shouldn't depend on the true state or which specific transect a card came from. `ae_zone` and `shape` are deliberately left free per state -- real, potentially state-dependent regional/dispersion effects, not detection artefacts. Full reasoning in `r/d_fit_plague_hmm.R`'s header.

## Fit diagnostics

```{r}
#| label: convergence

## Both models, side by side -- purrr::imap_dfr() over model_variants (setup chunk) rather than
## repeating this chunk once per model, so a third model variant later needs no new chunk here.
## AIC comes from fit_stats, computed at fit time: AIC() on a model reloaded from the store segfaults
## (r/d_fit_plague_hmm_subprocess.R).
conv_by_model <- purrr::imap_dfr(model_variants, function(m, label) {
  conv <- m$hmm$out()
  tibble::tibble(Model = label, Convergence = conv$convergence, Message = conv$message,
                 Iterations = conv$iterations, AIC = round(attr(m$hmm, "fit_stats")$aic, 1))
})
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-convergence

conv_by_model |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Optimiser convergence and AIC, by model") |>
  gt::tab_footnote("hmmTMB flags AIC as \"experimental for models with random effects or splines\" -- read as directional, not a precise figure.")
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-coeff

## One row per transition-formula parameter, one column per model -- a natural side-by-side read
## since both models share the exact same formula, differing only in which paddock-seasons are
## anchored.
coeff_by_model <- purrr::imap_dfr(model_variants, function(m, label) {
  hid_coeff <- m$hmm$hid()$coeff_fe()
  tibble::tibble(Model = label, Parameter = rownames(hid_coeff), Estimate = round(hid_coeff[, 1], 3))
})

coeff_by_model |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Model, values_from = Estimate) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(Supervised, Unsupervised), decimals = 3) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.8em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Transition model fixed-effect coefficients (logit scale), by model -- zone deviations shown separately below")
```

`rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak`'s own row is its coefficient in the reference zone (`NSW Central`, the level mgcv's interaction coding omits) -- see [Zone-specific deviations] for every zone's own slope. `gpp_rolling6` points the same direction for both transitions (higher 6-month GPP makes entering plague more likely, leaving it less likely). `soil_moisture` and `min_temp` are both treated as untested hypotheses, not yet checked against real plague-occurrence data the way `rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak` was (`quarto_reports/covariate_summary.qmd`'s whiplash-validation section) -- see [Known limitations].

### Zone-specific deviations

Two zone random effects sit on the transition probabilities -- an intercept (`s(ae_zone, bs = "re")`) and, since 2026-09, `rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak`'s own zone-varying slope (`s(ae_zone, by = rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak, bs = "re")`, replacing an earlier fixed `rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak:ae_zone` interaction -- see [Known limitations] and `r/d_fit_plague_hmm.R`'s header for why). Both do double duty: partial pooling for estimation (each zone's own deviation is shrunk toward the pooled/global value, not estimated as if it were its own independent model), and a diagnostic for whether the covariate-risk relationship is transportable to un-monitored zones -- homogeneous deviations support applying the pooled relationship nationally, substantial zone-to-zone spread is a warning against it. This section stays supervised-only (unlike most of this report) -- the zone random effect's own regional (NSW-vs-SA) split was validated against real plague-occurrence data specifically for the anchored model, and tripling these already-dense per-zone tables with a third dimension traded more clutter than insight; the unsupervised model's own version is one `model_variants$Unsupervised$hmm` swap away if needed later.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-zone-deviations

## re_coeff's own rownames mix TWO random effects (the intercept and rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak's
## own slope, both s(ae_zone, ...) terms) under the same "<Transition>.s(ae_zone)[...].{zone index}"
## naming -- distinguished here by whether the term itself carries ":rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak"
## (the slope) or not (the plain intercept), not just by trailing index, which both share.
zone_levels <- levels(hmm_data$ae_zone)
re_coeff <- plague_hmm$hid()$coeff_re()
re_rownames <- rownames(re_coeff)
intercept_rows <- grepl("s\\(ae_zone\\)\\.[0-9]+$", re_rownames)
zone_idx <- as.integer(sub(".*\\.", "", re_rownames[intercept_rows]))

tibble::tibble(
  Transition = sub("\\..*", "", re_rownames[intercept_rows]),
  `AE zone`   = zone_levels[zone_idx],
  Deviation   = round(re_coeff[intercept_rows, 1], 3)
) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Transition, values_from = Deviation) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(`S1>S2`, `S2>S1`), decimals = 3) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Zone-specific logit-scale intercept deviations (random effect) from the fixed-effect coefficients above")
```

Deviations here span `r round(min(re_coeff[intercept_rows, 1]), 2)` to `r round(max(re_coeff[intercept_rows, 1]), 2)` on the logit scale -- modest, not the extreme values a thin-data or degenerate fit produces elsewhere in this project (see `r/d_fit_plague_hmm.R`'s header for those cases).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-rain-whiplash-zone-slope

## rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak's own zone slope = the pooled fixed-effect coefficient (below, its
## row in coeff_fe()) PLUS each zone's own random-effect deviation (coeff_re(), the slope rows
## excluded from tbl-zone-deviations above) -- Pedersen et al.'s (2019, PeerJ 7:e6876) own "Model
## GS": a global slope plus group-level deviations pulled toward it by a shared penalty.
slope_rows <- grepl("s\\(ae_zone\\):rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak\\.[0-9]+$", re_rownames)
zone_idx_slope <- as.integer(sub(".*\\.", "", re_rownames[slope_rows]))

fe_coeff <- plague_hmm$hid()$coeff_fe()
pooled_slope <- fe_coeff[c("S1>S2.rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak", "S2>S1.rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak"), 1]
names(pooled_slope) <- c("S1>S2", "S2>S1")

whiplash_zone_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  Transition = sub("\\..*", "", re_rownames[slope_rows]),
  `AE zone`   = zone_levels[zone_idx_slope],
  Deviation   = re_coeff[slope_rows, 1]
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(`Total slope` = round(pooled_slope[Transition] + Deviation, 3), Deviation = round(Deviation, 3))

whiplash_zone_tbl |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Transition, values_from = c(Deviation, `Total slope`)) |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = dplyr::matches("^(Deviation|Total slope)_"), decimals = 3) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak's own zone-specific slope (deviation from, and combined with, the pooled coefficient above)")
```

`rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak`'s own zone-varying slope is a hierarchical random slope (partially pooled, not a fully independent per-zone estimate -- see the header note above), which is visible directly in how modest every zone's own deviation from the pooled estimate is (`r round(min(re_coeff[slope_rows, 1]), 2)` to `r round(max(re_coeff[slope_rows, 1]), 2)` on the logit scale, vs. the earlier fixed-interaction spec's own outliers documented in [Known limitations]). The South Australian zones' own `S1>S2` total slopes cluster toward the higher end (0.78-1.06), the same broad NSW-vs-SA split `soil_moisture`'s own pooled coefficient and random-intercept deviations show independently -- though `NSW NW Qld SW` (1.44) sits higher still, so this isn't a clean two-region split. WA's own 4 zones sit `r if (any(grepl("^WA", whiplash_zone_tbl[["AE zone"]]))) "within that same overall range, no standalone outlier" else "not yet in this table (add WA to hmm_states, _targets.R, and refit if they're missing)"` -- exactly the partial-pooling behaviour that makes their own inclusion viable at all (see [Known limitations] for the earlier, fixed-interaction version's own identifiability failure on two of these same 4 zones).

### Covariate effects on transition probability

```{r}
#| label: covariate-effects-by-zone-data

transition_covariates <- c("rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak", "gpp_rolling6", "soil_moisture", "min_temp")
covariate_labels <- c(
  rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak = "Rainfall whiplash",
  gpp_rolling6                 = "GPP (6-month rolling)",
  soil_moisture                = "Soil moisture",
  min_temp                     = "Minimum temperature"
)

## Hold every covariate except the one being varied at ITS OWN median (hmm_data, the data actually
## fit to) -- a realistic combination of conditions, not an arbitrary reference point. season fixed
## at "Spring" purely because $predict() validates every formula's covariates are present
## (r/d_predict_plague_risk.R's own header explains this hmmTMB behaviour) -- season has no bearing
## on the transition-side prediction actually being computed here.
covariate_medians <- sapply(transition_covariates, function(cv) median(hmm_data[[cv]], na.rm = TRUE))

## One curve per covariate x zone combination -- ae_zone genuinely affects this prediction (zone
## random intercept), so a single "representative" zone would hide real regional variation
## ([Zone-specific deviations] above). n_post draws hmmTMB's own posterior samples of the
## fixed+random-effect coefficients (HMM$predict()'s own mechanism) for a genuine (not delta-method)
## 95% CI -- seeded once so bands are reproducible across re-renders.
set.seed(20260807)

## Every observation-formula covariate NOT already a real per-cell column below (season, ae_zone)
## is auto-filled from the fitted model's own training mean/reference level -- same introspection-
## based mechanism as r/d_predict_plague_risk.R (its own header explains why this replaced a hand-
## maintained placeholder list: it silently fell out of sync once burrow_count's formula grew
## gpp_finescale/summer_zone_ne, confirmed live to break this exact $predict() call with "object
## 'gpp_finescale' not found" -- caught by actually rendering this report, not just parsing it).
## None of this affects the "tpm" quantity actually being predicted here.
obs_training_data <- plague_hmm$obs()$data()
obs_vars <- unique(unlist(lapply(plague_hmm$obs()$formulas(), function(param_list) {
  unlist(lapply(param_list, function(state_list) unlist(lapply(state_list, all.vars))))
})))

covariate_effects_by_zone <- purrr::map_dfr(transition_covariates, function(cv) {
  qs <- quantile(hmm_data[[cv]], probs = c(0.05, 0.95), na.rm = TRUE)
  seq_vals <- seq(qs[1], qs[2], length.out = 60)

  purrr::map_dfr(zone_levels, function(zn) {
    nd <- as.data.frame(matrix(rep(covariate_medians, each = length(seq_vals)),
                                nrow = length(seq_vals), dimnames = list(NULL, transition_covariates)))
    nd[[cv]] <- seq_vals
    nd$season <- factor("Spring", levels = c("Summer", "Autumn", "Winter", "Spring"), ordered = TRUE)
    nd$ae_zone <- factor(zn, levels = zone_levels)
    for (v in setdiff(obs_vars, names(nd))) {
      nd[[v]] <- if (is.factor(obs_training_data[[v]])) {
        factor(levels(obs_training_data[[v]])[1], levels = levels(obs_training_data[[v]]))
      } else {
        mean(obs_training_data[[v]], na.rm = TRUE)
      }
    }

    tpm_pred <- plague_hmm$predict(what = "tpm", newdata = nd, n_post = 500, level = 0.95)
    tibble::tibble(
      covariate   = cv,
      ae_zone     = zn,
      value       = rep(seq_vals, 2),
      transition  = rep(c("Entering plague", "Leaving plague"), each = length(seq_vals)),
      probability = c(tpm_pred$mle["state 1", "state 2", ], tpm_pred$mle["state 2", "state 1", ]),
      ci_low      = c(tpm_pred$lcl["state 1", "state 2", ], tpm_pred$lcl["state 2", "state 1", ]),
      ci_high     = c(tpm_pred$ucl["state 1", "state 2", ], tpm_pred$ucl["state 2", "state 1", ])
    )
  })
}) |>
  dplyr::mutate(covariate_label = factor(covariate_labels[covariate], levels = covariate_labels))

covariate_rug <- purrr::map_dfr(transition_covariates, function(cv) {
  tibble::tibble(covariate_label = covariate_labels[cv], value = hmm_data[[cv]])
}) |>
  dplyr::mutate(covariate_label = factor(covariate_label, levels = covariate_labels))

## RColorBrewer's "Dark2" qualitative palette caps at 8 distinct colours -- 11 zones since WA joined
## the fit (2026-09) exceeds that, so colorRampPalette() interpolates the extra colours needed from
## Dark2's own 8-colour base rather than switching palettes entirely (confirmed live: brewer.pal()
## itself silently returns only 8 colours past its own max, with no error, which is what broke
## setNames() below with a length-8-vs-11 mismatch).
zone_colours <- setNames(
  grDevices::colorRampPalette(RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8, "Dark2"))(length(zone_levels)),
  zone_levels
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-covariate-effects-entering
#| fig-cap: "Predicted Pr(state 1 -> state 2), \"entering plague\", as each transition covariate varies across its own 5th-95th percentile range, holding the other three at their own median -- one line per AE zone, using that zone's own fitted random-intercept deviation. Shaded bands are 95% CIs from 500 posterior draws. Rug marks show observed data density -- sparser regions are more extrapolated."
#| fig-asp: 0.45

ggplot(dplyr::filter(covariate_effects_by_zone, transition == "Entering plague"),
       aes(value, probability, colour = ae_zone, fill = ae_zone)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high), colour = NA, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_rug(data = covariate_rug, aes(x = value), inherit.aes = FALSE, sides = "b", alpha = 0.05) +
  facet_wrap(~covariate_label, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = zone_colours, name = "AE zone") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = zone_colours, name = "AE zone") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Pr(entering plague)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2), fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-covariate-effects-leaving
#| fig-cap: "Predicted Pr(state 2 -> state 1), \"leaving plague\", same covariate ranges, zone colours and CI construction as the entering-plague panel above."
#| fig-asp: 0.45

ggplot(dplyr::filter(covariate_effects_by_zone, transition == "Leaving plague"),
       aes(value, probability, colour = ae_zone, fill = ae_zone)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high), colour = NA, alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_rug(data = covariate_rug, aes(x = value), inherit.aes = FALSE, sides = "b", alpha = 0.05) +
  facet_wrap(~covariate_label, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = zone_colours, name = "AE zone") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = zone_colours, name = "AE zone") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Pr(leaving plague)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2), fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

Each panel isolates one covariate's own marginal effect, everything else held fixed -- these read the fitted coefficients above directly as probabilities, but don't capture interactions between the four covariates. CI bands widen toward each covariate's own extremes (fewer observations that far from the median) and differ by zone, tracking each zone's own data volume. The South Australian zones sit visibly higher on entering-plague risk and lower on leaving-plague probability than the NSW zones across every covariate -- the same regional split [Zone-specific deviations] shows in coefficient form. `rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak` and `gpp_rolling6` show the expected monotonic pattern (entering-plague risk rises, leaving-plague risk falls, as each increases); `soil_moisture`'s entering-plague curve now rises too (consistent with its coefficient's own sign, [Fit diagnostics]), though its leaving-plague curve still rises with wetter conditions; `min_temp` shows both curves falling as temperature rises.

## Observation model

```{r}
#| label: tbl-obspar

obs_par <- plague_hmm$obs()$par(t = 1)[, , 1]
keep_rows <- !grepl(paste(chewcard_streams[-1], collapse = "|"), rownames(obs_par))
as.data.frame(obs_par[keep_rows, , drop = FALSE]) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("Parameter") |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(`state 1`, `state 2`), decimals = 3) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Observation distribution parameters (row 1 of hmm_data -- mean/prob also vary by season and search effort, this is one snapshot)")
```

`chewcard_block2/3/4` are omitted from the table above -- every one of their own parameters is numerically identical to `chewcard_count`'s by construction (tied, see [Model specification]), so showing all four would only repeat the same row three times. `chewcard_count.size` stays fixed at 10 in every block (the trials parameter isn't estimated); `chewcard_count.prob` shows a large, well-separated state contrast, a strong signal.

```{r}
#| label: fig-season-effects
#| fig-cap: "Fitted mean (trap_count, burrow_count) or detection probability (chewcard_count) by season and state -- the detection-side ~season formula each stream carries, not a plague-risk signal."

season_levels_obs <- levels(hmm_data$season)
season_row_idx <- sapply(season_levels_obs, function(s) which(hmm_data$season == s)[1])
obs_par_by_season <- plague_hmm$obs()$par(t = season_row_idx)

season_effects <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(season_levels_obs), function(i) {
  tibble::tibble(
    season = season_levels_obs[i],
    stream = c("trap_count", "trap_count", "burrow_count", "burrow_count", "chewcard_count", "chewcard_count"),
    state  = rep(c("state 1", "state 2"), 3),
    value  = c(
      obs_par_by_season["trap_count.mean", , i],
      obs_par_by_season["burrow_count.mean", , i],
      obs_par_by_season["chewcard_count.prob", , i]
    )
  )
})

stream_labels <- c(trap_count = "trap_count.mean", burrow_count = "burrow_count.mean", chewcard_count = "chewcard_count.prob")

ggplot(season_effects, aes(factor(season, levels = season_levels_obs), value, colour = state, group = state)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  facet_wrap(~stream, scales = "free_y", labeller = as_labeller(stream_labels)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`state 1` = "#2166ac", `state 2` = hazard_colors[5]), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Fitted value") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

`burrow_count.mean` shows the clearest, most biologically legible pattern -- lowest in Spring, highest in Autumn (post-harvest bare ground vs. dense winter-crop cover near flowering). Note the season effect is tied across states by design (see [Model specification]) -- the lines differ in *level* (the state-specific intercept) but trace an identical seasonal *shape*.

### Distribution family review

`nbinom2` (mean/shape) is used for `trap_count`/`burrow_count`; alternatives better suited to genuinely proportional data (`beta`/`zoibeta` on the capped success rate, hurdle negative binomial) were tried and rejected -- either non-functional in the installed hmmTMB build or numerically incompatible with the search-effort offset both streams need. `chewcard_count`'s varying card counts (10/20/40 depending on transects deployed) are handled with 4 tied beta-binomial(10) streams rather than one variable-trials stream, since hmmTMB's own trials parameter can't vary by covariate -- confirmed against the package's own `crossbill_occupancy.R` case study as its documented pattern for this exact problem, not a workaround. The beta-binomial (`betabinom`, the family `chewcard_count_exploration.qmd` recommends) lets the chew probability vary between sessions, so cards within a session are chewed together more often than independent binomial trials allow; it isn't in CRAN hmmTMB 1.1.2 and comes from the patched build pinned in `renv.lock` (github.com/matt-w-rees/hmmTMB, branch `betabinom-dev`: hmmTMB's development version plus the family). Full investigation, including every family/distribution ruled out and why: `r/d_fit_plague_hmm.R`'s header.

## Pseudo-residuals

```{r}
#| label: pseudores

## Randomised pseudo-residuals (r/d_randomised_pseudores.R), computed once as their own target.
pr <- plague_hmm_pseudores
pr_summary <- purrr::imap_dfr(pr, function(x, nm) {
  x <- x[is.finite(x)]
  tibble::tibble(Stream = nm, n = length(x), Mean = mean(x), SD = sd(x),
                 `% |z|>2` = 100*mean(abs(x) > 2))
})
pr_summary |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(Mean, SD, `% |z|>2`), decimals = 2) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em")
```

These are randomised quantile pseudo-residuals (`r/d_randomised_pseudores.R`): hmmTMB's own `pseudores()` evaluates the forecast CDF at the observation itself, which for count data shifts residuals upward and compresses them even when the model is correct (mean ~0.5, SD ~0.7 on simulated, correctly specified data), so it can't be read against the usual standard-normal target. A well-fit stream should show mean &asymp; 0, SD &asymp; 1 and about 5% beyond ±2. `r calibrated <- pr_summary$Stream[abs(pr_summary$Mean) < 0.1 & abs(pr_summary$SD - 1) < 0.1]; miscal <- setdiff(pr_summary$Stream, calibrated); paste0(if (length(calibrated)) paste0("Well calibrated: ", paste0("\x60", calibrated, "\x60", collapse = ", "), ". ") else "", if (length(miscal)) paste0("Not well calibrated: ", paste0("\x60", miscal, "\x60", collapse = ", "), " -- SD ", paste(sprintf("%.2f", pr_summary$SD[pr_summary$Stream %in% miscal]), collapse = "/"), ", i.e. more spread than the family allows.") else "")`

### Posterior-predictive check

The pseudo-residuals above are a per-row diagnostic. This section (2026-09, following a review of the HMM-diagnostics literature -- Glennie et al. 2023, *Methods in Ecology and Evolution*, "Hidden Markov models: pitfalls and opportunities in ecology") is a genuinely different lens: simulate whole replicate datasets FROM the fitted model (`hmmTMB`'s own `HMM$check()` -- a purpose-built parametric-bootstrap mechanism, confirmed via the installed package's own help pages rather than hand-rolled) and check whether basic real-data summary statistics look like a plausible draw from what the model itself actually generates, not just whether each row's own quantile residual looks standard-normal.

```{r}
#| label: ppc-summary

## plague_hmm_ppc (r/d_check_plague_hmm_fit.R, _targets.R) -- 100 replicate datasets simulated
## from plague_hmm itself, holding every row's real covariates fixed. A real, non-obvious pitfall
## had to be fixed before this was usable at all: HMM$simulate() fills in a value at EVERY row,
## not just the ones with a real observation (confirmed live, r/d_check_plague_hmm_fit.R's own
## header) -- so every statistic below is computed after masking simulated data back to the SAME
## real missingness pattern, on both sides of the comparison.
##
## pctile is where the real value falls within its own 100 simulated replicates -- 0 or 1 means
## the real data sits outside the ENTIRE simulated range, the strongest signal 100 simulations can
## give. p_value is the usual two-sided posterior-predictive read of that (either tail is equally
## informative -- real data running higher OR lower than every simulation both indicate
## miscalibration), floored at 1/n_sims since 100 replicates can't resolve anything finer.
ppc_pctile <- plague_hmm_ppc$simulated |>
  dplyr::left_join(plague_hmm_ppc$observed, by = "statistic") |>
  dplyr::group_by(statistic) |>
  dplyr::summarise(pctile = mean(simulated <= observed), n_sims = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

ppc_summary <- plague_hmm_ppc$simulated |>
  dplyr::group_by(statistic) |>
  dplyr::summarise(sim_mean = mean(simulated), sim_sd = sd(simulated), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(plague_hmm_ppc$observed, by = "statistic") |>
  dplyr::left_join(ppc_pctile, by = "statistic") |>
  dplyr::mutate(p_value = pmax(2 * pmin(pctile, 1 - pctile), 1 / n_sims)) |>
  dplyr::select(statistic, observed, sim_mean, sim_sd, pctile, p_value)

get_stat <- function(s, col) round(ppc_summary[[col]][ppc_summary$statistic == s], 3)

## n_outside_range/n_statistics computed live for the figure's own caption below (not transcribed
## -- this project's own history has at least one caught case of a hand-typed number drifting out
## of sync with the live table it described, quarto_reports/plague_model_summary.qmd's own
## known-limitations-stats chunk). pctile exactly 0 or 1 means the real value sits outside the
## ENTIRE range of 100 simulated replicates -- the strongest signal that many simulations can give.
n_outside_range <- sum(ppc_summary$pctile %in% c(0, 1))
n_statistics <- nrow(ppc_summary)
ppc_histograms_caption <- paste0(
  "Each panel: 100 values of one summary statistic, simulated from `plague_hmm` itself (grey bars), ",
  "against the real observed value (red line) -- both computed over the identical set of genuinely-",
  "surveyed rows (see code comment for why that match matters). The real value sits outside the ",
  "entire simulated range for ", n_outside_range, " of ", n_statistics, " statistics here -- the ",
  "strongest signal 100 replicates can give that the fitted model doesn't reproduce that specific ",
  "feature of the real data."
)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-ppc-histograms
#| fig-cap: !expr ppc_histograms_caption
#| fig-asp: 0.85

ggplot(plague_hmm_ppc$simulated, aes(simulated)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "grey75", colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_vline(data = plague_hmm_ppc$observed, aes(xintercept = observed), colour = hazard_colors[5], linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~statistic, scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Simulated replicates") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ppc-summary

ppc_summary |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(observed, sim_mean, sim_sd), decimals = 3) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = pctile, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::fmt_scientific(columns = p_value, decimals = 1) |>
  gt::cols_label(statistic = "Statistic", observed = "Real value", sim_mean = "Simulated mean",
                 sim_sd = "Simulated SD", pctile = "Percentile of real value", p_value = "p-value") |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.8em")
```

The check shows:

- **`burrow_count`'s real mean and SD (`r get_stat("burrow_count: mean", "observed")`, `r get_stat("burrow_count: SD", "observed")`) sit BELOW every one of the 100 simulated replicates** (simulated mean `r get_stat("burrow_count: mean", "sim_mean")`, SD `r get_stat("burrow_count: SD", "sim_mean")`) -- the fitted model, actually simulated forward, generates noticeably higher and more variable burrow counts than real surveys ever show. `nbinom2`'s own `shape` parameter (overdispersion) is the natural suspect: a heavy-tailed fit lets rare, very large simulated draws inflate both the simulated mean and SD well past what real data ever produces, even though most real (and simulated) values sit near zero.
- **`trap_count` runs the opposite way** -- the real mean (`r get_stat("trap_count: mean", "observed")` vs. a simulated mean of `r get_stat("trap_count: mean", "sim_mean")`) sits above all 100 simulated replicates (percentile `r get_stat("trap_count: mean", "pctile")`), and the real SD (`r get_stat("trap_count: SD", "observed")` vs. simulated `r get_stat("trap_count: SD", "sim_mean")`) sits above all but one (percentile `r get_stat("trap_count: SD", "pctile")`) -- the model under-predicts both the level and the spread of real trap catches. `trap_count`'s pseudo-residuals are well calibrated, so this is a whole-dataset shortfall (the largest catches) rather than a row-by-row misfit.
- **`chewcard_count`'s boundary frequencies are reproduced** -- the real Pr(0 cards chewed) (`r get_stat("chewcard_count: Pr(0)", "observed")`) and Pr(all 10 chewed) (`r get_stat("chewcard_count: Pr(10)", "observed")`) sit at the `r round(100 * get_stat("chewcard_count: Pr(0)", "pctile"))`th and `r round(100 * get_stat("chewcard_count: Pr(10)", "pctile"))`th percentiles of the simulations (simulated means `r get_stat("chewcard_count: Pr(0)", "sim_mean")` and `r get_stat("chewcard_count: Pr(10)", "sim_mean")`). The beta-binomial's overdispersion captures sessions landing at 'nothing touched' or 'everything touched', which independent binomial trials can't.

The remaining misfit is in traps and burrows: `nbinom2` can't fully represent real biological clustering (recaptures and aggregation) in the rarest, largest counts, and their pseudo-residuals are well calibrated row by row. See [Known limitations] for where this leaves the model's practical reliability.

## Validation against known history

This section (through [Spatial pattern in key years]), and [Observation model]/[Pseudo-residuals] above, stay supervised-only for now -- same scope decision as [Zone-specific deviations], stated once here rather than repeated at each heading. `plague_hmm`/`state_probs_df`/`by_year` thread through several paragraphs of prose with many inline computed numbers each; genuinely dualising them means rewriting that narrative, not swapping an object name, and isn't done yet while the underlying pipeline is still mid-rebuild anyway (`model_variants`'s own current numbers, `plague_hmm` included, are themselves not final -- see [Overview]). `model_variants` (setup chunk) is there to make this section's own eventual dual-model version straightforward when it's next revisited.

The state anchors trivially agree with themselves once fit (hmmTMB fixes known states during estimation), so that's not a real check. The informative test is whether the model's own state estimate -- across *every* paddock-season, not just anchored ones -- lines up with genuinely declared plague years it was never directly told about at most paddocks.

```{r}
#| label: fig-viterbi-by-year
#| fig-cap: "Mean smoothed Pr(plague state) across all paddock-seasons, by year, against calendar years yearly_plague_occurrence.csv flags for at least one state. Pre-2014 years have no anchor at all, so every bar in that range is pure free estimate."

state_probs_df <- hmm_data |>
  mutate(
    year_adj = as.integer(sub(".*-", "", as.character(season_year_adj))),
    state2_prob = plague_hmm$state_probs()[, "state2"]
  )

flagged_years <- yearly_plague_occurrence |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-Year, names_to = "state", values_to = "flag") |>
  filter(!is.na(flag), flag == 1) |>
  distinct(Year) |>
  pull(Year)

by_year <- state_probs_df |>
  group_by(year_adj) |>
  summarise(mean_state2_prob = mean(state2_prob), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(flagged = year_adj %in% flagged_years)

ggplot(by_year, aes(year_adj, mean_state2_prob, fill = flagged)) +
  geom_col() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = hazard_colors[5], `FALSE` = "grey75"),
                     labels = c(`TRUE` = "Flagged plague year (≥ 1 state)", `FALSE` = "Not flagged"),
                     name = NULL) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean Pr(plague state) across all paddock-seasons") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r}
#| label: viterbi-2010-2011

## Baseline and hard-decode figures for the 2010-2011 discussion below -- computed live rather
## than transcribed, so they can't silently drift out of sync with whichever model this report
## currently loads.
baseline_2008 <- round(mean(state_probs_df$state2_prob[state_probs_df$year_adj == 2008]), 3)
vit <- plague_hmm$viterbi()
vit_2010_pct <- round(100 * mean(vit[state_probs_df$year_adj == 2010] == 2), 1)
vit_2011_pct <- round(100 * mean(vit[state_probs_df$year_adj == 2011] == 2), 1)

## Mean smoothed Pr(plague state) for every year recent_plague_maps directly anchors -- computed
## live over mapped_years (Data and anchoring, above) rather than hard-coded to whichever specific
## years happened to be anchored under the superseded (a)+(b) rule.
mapped_year_probs <- state_probs_df |>
  filter(year_adj %in% mapped_years) |>
  group_by(year_adj) |>
  summarise(mean_prob = mean(state2_prob), .groups = "drop")
mapped_year_probs_str <- paste(
  sprintf("%d (%s)", mapped_year_probs$year_adj, scales::percent(mapped_year_probs$mean_prob, accuracy = 1)),
  collapse = ", "
)
```

**2010-2011 is the most informative test of blind forecasting the panel offers.** Both years have **zero observation data of any kind** (`trap_count`/`burrow_count`/`chewcard_count` all completely NA across every paddock that period -- rapid assessment hadn't started, no live-trapping recorded nationally), so this is a fully blind, two-season-long forecast: nothing but the covariate-driven transition mechanism, propagated forward with no observation correction, can move the state estimate here. `rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak` spiked unusually across the four eastern states through 2010-2011 (confirmed live: NSW/QLD/SA/VIC each roughly doubled or more from 2010 to 2011 -- WA's own values don't show the same pattern, and WA wasn't part of the panel when this finding was first documented), and the mean smoothed Pr(plague state) rose accordingly -- from a `r baseline_2008` baseline in 2008 to **`r round(mean(state_probs_df$state2_prob[state_probs_df$year_adj == 2010]), 3)`** in 2010 and **`r round(mean(state_probs_df$state2_prob[state_probs_df$year_adj == 2011]), 3)`** in 2011, comparable to 2021's own `r round(mean(state_probs_df$state2_prob[state_probs_df$year_adj == 2021]), 3)`, both years the model *is* directly anchored to. The hard Viterbi decode is less convincing on its own (`r vit_2010_pct`%/`r vit_2011_pct`% for 2010/2011, since the elevated probability mostly doesn't cross the implicit 50% most-likely-state threshold) -- a real limitation of reading a hard decode alone, not a sign the underlying estimate is uninformative.

The years recent_plague_maps directly anchors (see [Data and anchoring]) show mean smoothed Pr(plague state) of `r mapped_year_probs_str` -- worth reading against the whole series, not assumed elevated by construction the way a within-season anchor point trivially is (this is a year-level *average* across every paddock, most of them unanchored that year). The 1985-`r first_mapped_year - 1` stretch is entirely free-estimated (no anchor at all) and mostly shows low, plausible percentages rather than a runaway collapse -- a reassuring sign in its own right, though none of it is validated against any anchor.

### Spatial pattern in key years

```{r}
#| label: fig-spatial-key-years
#| fig-cap: !expr spatial_key_years_caption
#| fig-asp: 0.55

## "Key years" = the 8 highest mean smoothed Pr(plague state) years from by_year above -- derived
## live from the fit itself, not cherry-picked. One point per paddock x key-year (mean state2_prob
## across that paddock's own seasons within the year).
key_years <- by_year |>
  slice_max(mean_state2_prob, n = 8) |>
  arrange(year_adj) |>
  pull(year_adj)

paddock_year_probs <- state_probs_df |>
  filter(year_adj %in% key_years) |>
  group_by(ID, year_adj, longitude, latitude) |>
  summarise(mean_state2_prob = mean(state2_prob), .groups = "drop")

spatial_key_years_caption <- paste0(
  "Mean smoothed Pr(plague state) by paddock, faceted across the ", length(key_years),
  " years with the highest national mean probability (", paste(key_years, collapse = ", "),
  ") -- derived live from by_year above. Grey polygons are the fitted AE zones."
)

fit_zones_ll <- st_transform(fit_zones_sf, 4326)
zones_bbox <- st_bbox(fit_zones_ll)

## GRDC growing subregions (a finer grain than ae_zone, see CLAUDE.md) clipped to the fitted
## zones' own union -- used by fig-predictor-maps below. Clipping (not just filtering by
## st_intersects()) matters here: several national subregion polygons extend well beyond the
## fitted zones (e.g. into WA or the desert interior), and an unclipped polygon would paint that
## entire unmonitored area with whatever mean value its own small overlapping sliver produced --
## confirmed live, a real visual bug on the first attempt, not a hypothetical one. sf_use_s2(FALSE)
## for the intersection matches attach_grdc_subregion()'s own convention (r/a_attach_grdc_subregion.R).
s2_was_on <- sf::sf_use_s2()
suppressMessages(sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE))
grdc_subregion_ll <- st_transform(grdc_subregion_adj, 4326) |>
  sf::st_intersection(sf::st_union(fit_zones_ll)) |>
  suppressMessages() |>
  suppressWarnings()
suppressMessages(sf::sf_use_s2(s2_was_on))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = fit_zones_ll, fill = "grey95", colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = aus_sf, fill = NA, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = paddock_year_probs, aes(longitude, latitude, colour = mean_state2_prob),
             size = 1.1, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_gradientn(colors = hazard_colors, limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent,
                          name = "Mean Pr(plague state)") +
  facet_wrap(~year_adj, ncol = 4) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(zones_bbox["xmin"], zones_bbox["xmax"]),
           ylim = c(zones_bbox["ymin"], zones_bbox["ymax"]), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(1.4, "cm"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

Coverage matters as much as risk here: earlier key years have fewer, more scattered points -- fewer paddocks had panel presence that far back. Where recent_plague_maps' own mapped years (`r paste(mapped_years, collapse = ", ")`) appear among these facets, elevated colour is partly anchor pull by construction; a non-anchored year showing elevated, spatially-clustered colour (rather than diffuse noise) is the more informative signal.

### Full-model onset skill

Everything above shows the model's own state estimate tracking real plague evidence *qualitatively* (the anchor-vs-model line chart, the 2010-2011 blind-forecast narrative, the by-year bar chart). This section turns that into single numbers -- does the model's own predicted Pr(entering plague) actually discriminate a real subsequent onset from a real non-onset, and how does that compare to the individual-covariate AUCs `covariate_summary.qmd`'s own [whiplash validation](covariate_summary.html#sec-whiplash-validation) already established (rain whiplash 0.717, soil moisture whiplash 0.714)? Added 2026-09, following a review of the forecasting-verification literature -- no equivalent existed for the full fitted model before this, only for individual raw covariates.

```{r}
#| label: onset-skill-data

## plague_hmm$predict(what = "tpm", newdata = hmm_data), evaluated at hmm_data's OWN rows (its own
## training data, so every covariate/factor level is already present -- unlike r/d_predict_plague_
## risk.R's grid prediction, no placeholder-filling is needed here), gives each paddock-season's own
## predicted Pr(state 1 -> state 2) -- exactly the quantity the risk map itself reports, evaluated
## where a real subsequent outcome is actually known. Two grains below, both computed for both
## models (model_variants) -- they answer genuinely different questions and are NOT meant to agree:
##
## (1) Paddock-season grain, matched to this project's OWN anchor rule (r/c_anchor_plague_state.R).
## For each paddock-season row NOT itself already anchored to the plague state (state != 2 -- i.e.
## genuinely "eligible to enter"; a row already anchored plague is a persistence continuation, which
## the LEAVING-plague transition governs, not this one, so including it here would test the wrong
## direction), does its predicted Pr(enter) discriminate whether the very next row for that same
## paddock (chronologically, hmmTMB's own unit of time -- not necessarily the immediately following
## calendar season, if a paddock wasn't surveyed every season) was itself anchored plague or not?
## This tests the model against the same evidentiary standard the whole report's anchoring already
## rests on, so strong separation here mostly confirms internal consistency (the model was fit to
## reproduce these same anchors, not a genuine held-out sample) rather than proving out-of-sample
## skill -- still informative (the unsupervised comparison below shows this is a real, non-trivial
## bar to clear), just not a substitute for grain (2).
##
## (2) State x calendar-year grain, deliberately reusing covariate_summary.qmd's own
## evaluate_onset() methodology (an eligible, non-refractory year predicting a NEW onset the
## FOLLOWING year, per raw yearly_plague_occurrence.csv alone -- condition (a), not this project's
## own stricter (a)+(b) anchor rule) so the resulting AUC is directly comparable to the 0.717/0.714
## already reported there for rain/soil-moisture whiplash alone. value_max is the model's own
## predicted Pr(enter), maximised across every paddock-season in that state-year (mirroring the
## covariate test's own "annual max" aggregation of a single raw covariate). This grain has a real
## limit worth stating plainly, not just the small onset count: it's restricted to state-years where
## hmm_data actually has paddock coverage at all -- a real, disclosed difference from the covariate-
## level test, which used the raw national covariate raster's own full 1983-2024 coverage with no
## such gap. See "State x calendar-year onset skill" below for the actual results and how to read
## them alongside the covariate-level benchmark.
##
## eligible_by_model (not just its own summary) is kept, not discarded after onset_skill_by_model is
## built -- "Translating risk into an operational threshold" (Prediction: current risk map, below)
## reuses model_variants$Supervised's own eligible/p_enter pairs directly, rather than recomputing
## the same $predict() call a second time.
auc_fn <- function(yes, no) {
  r <- rank(c(yes, no))
  (sum(r[seq_along(yes)]) - length(yes) * (length(yes) + 1) / 2) / (length(yes) * length(no))
}

eligible_by_model <- purrr::imap(model_variants, function(m, label) {
  p_enter <- m$hmm$predict(what = "tpm", newdata = hmm_data)["state 1", "state 2", ]
  hmm_data |>
    dplyr::mutate(p_enter = p_enter) |>
    dplyr::arrange(ID, season_year_adj) |>
    dplyr::group_by(ID) |>
    dplyr::mutate(next_state = dplyr::lead(state)) |>
    dplyr::ungroup() |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(next_state), is.na(state) | state != 2)
})

onset_skill_by_model <- purrr::imap_dfr(eligible_by_model, function(eligible, label) {
  yes <- eligible$p_enter[eligible$next_state == 2]
  no  <- eligible$p_enter[eligible$next_state == 1]
  tibble::tibble(
    Model = label, `n (onset)` = length(yes), `n (stayed clear)` = length(no),
    `Median Pr(enter) | onset` = median(yes), `Median Pr(enter) | stayed clear` = median(no),
    AUC = auc_fn(yes, no), `p-value` = t.test(yes, no)$p.value
  )
})

## Plain, syntactic scalar names for the inline prose below -- markdown's own single-backtick
## inline-code delimiter can't contain a literal backtick, so a non-syntactic column name (e.g.
## `n (onset)`) can never be referenced directly inside a `r ...` inline span; extracting into a
## bare variable here, once, is the fix (same convention baseline_2008/vit_2010_pct etc. already
## use elsewhere in this document for the identical reason).
sup_auc_paddock      <- onset_skill_by_model$AUC[1]
unsup_auc_paddock    <- onset_skill_by_model$AUC[2]
sup_n_onset_paddock  <- onset_skill_by_model$`n (onset)`[1]
sup_n_clear_paddock  <- onset_skill_by_model$`n (stayed clear)`[1]
sup_median_onset     <- onset_skill_by_model$`Median Pr(enter) | onset`[1]
sup_median_clear     <- onset_skill_by_model$`Median Pr(enter) | stayed clear`[1]
unsup_median_onset   <- onset_skill_by_model$`Median Pr(enter) | onset`[2]
unsup_median_clear   <- onset_skill_by_model$`Median Pr(enter) | stayed clear`[2]
unsup_p_paddock      <- onset_skill_by_model$`p-value`[2]
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-onset-skill

onset_skill_by_model |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(`Median Pr(enter) | onset`, `Median Pr(enter) | stayed clear`, AUC), decimals = 3) |>
  gt::fmt_scientific(columns = `p-value`, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Paddock-season onset discrimination: predicted Pr(enter) vs. the very next season's real anchor")
```

The supervised model's own predicted Pr(entering plague) is a real, substantial discriminator of the very next season's anchored outcome (AUC = **`r round(sup_auc_paddock, 3)`**, `r sup_n_onset_paddock` real onsets vs. `r sup_n_clear_paddock` seasons that stayed clear, median predicted risk `r scales::percent(sup_median_onset, accuracy = 0.1)` before a real onset vs. `r scales::percent(sup_median_clear, accuracy = 0.1)` before one that stayed clear). The unsupervised model, evaluated exactly the same way, does not (AUC = **`r round(unsup_auc_paddock, 3)`**) -- its own median predicted risk actually runs the *wrong* way (`r scales::percent(unsup_median_onset, accuracy = 0.1)` before onset vs. `r scales::percent(unsup_median_clear, accuracy = 0.1)` before staying clear), a real, statistically significant reversal (p = `r formatC(unsup_p_paddock, format = "e", digits = 2)`), not noise scattered around 0.5. Read together with [Overview]'s own framing: the unsupervised model's freely-discovered 2-state split reflects *some* real structure in the trap/burrow/chewcard data, but not specifically "plague or not" -- it takes the anchors to align state 2 with genuine plague risk at all, a sharper, quantified version of the qualitative gap [Anchored states vs. the model's own estimate, by state] already shows.

```{r}
#| label: annual-skill-data

## Same evaluate_onset() methodology as covariate_summary.qmd's own whiplash-plague-validation-table
## chunk, reused here (not sourced -- this document stays self-contained, same convention as every
## other quarto report in this project) so the resulting AUC sits on the identical scale as the
## 0.717/0.714 already reported there. plague_long/recent_plague are rebuilt from yearly_plague_
## occurrence (already tar_load()'d, setup chunk) rather than tar_load()'d themselves, since
## covariate_summary.qmd computes them from the raw CSV directly too, not as their own targets.
state_lookup <- c("South Australia" = "SA", "Victoria" = "VIC", "New South Wales" = "NSW", "Queensland" = "QLD")
plague_long <- yearly_plague_occurrence |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-Year, names_to = "state_full", values_to = "flag") |>
  dplyr::mutate(state = state_lookup[state_full], plague = !is.na(flag) & flag == 1) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(state)) |>
  dplyr::select(year = Year, state, plague) |>
  dplyr::filter(year >= 1983, year <= 2024)

plague_years_by_state <- plague_long |> dplyr::filter(plague) |> dplyr::select(state, plague_year = year)
all_state_years <- tidyr::expand_grid(state = unique(hmm_data$aus_state), year = 1983:2024)
recent_plague <- all_state_years |>
  dplyr::left_join(plague_years_by_state, by = "state", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  dplyr::mutate(years_since = year - plague_year) |>
  dplyr::group_by(state, year) |>
  dplyr::summarise(in_refractory_window = any(years_since %in% 1:2, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

annual_skill_by_model <- purrr::imap_dfr(model_variants, function(m, label) {
  p_enter <- m$hmm$predict(what = "tpm", newdata = hmm_data)["state 1", "state 2", ]
  annual_model <- hmm_data |>
    dplyr::mutate(p_enter = p_enter) |>
    dplyr::group_by(state = aus_state, year = year_adj) |>
    dplyr::summarise(value_max = max(p_enter, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
  onset_test <- annual_model |>
    dplyr::inner_join(plague_long, by = c("state", "year")) |> dplyr::filter(!plague) |>
    dplyr::inner_join(recent_plague, by = c("state", "year")) |> dplyr::filter(!in_refractory_window) |>
    dplyr::mutate(match_year = year + 1) |>
    dplyr::inner_join(plague_long, by = c("state", "match_year" = "year"), suffix = c("_this", "_next")) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(value_max))
  yes <- onset_test$value_max[onset_test$plague_next]
  no  <- onset_test$value_max[!onset_test$plague_next]
  tibble::tibble(Model = label, `n (onset)` = length(yes), `n (no onset)` = length(no),
                 AUC = auc_fn(yes, no), `p-value` = t.test(yes, no)$p.value)
})

## Plain scalar names again, same reason as onset-skill-data's own note above.
sup_auc_annual     <- annual_skill_by_model$AUC[1]
unsup_auc_annual   <- annual_skill_by_model$AUC[2]
sup_n_onset_annual <- annual_skill_by_model$`n (onset)`[1]
sup_n_no_annual    <- annual_skill_by_model$`n (no onset)`[1]
sup_p_annual       <- annual_skill_by_model$`p-value`[1]
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-annual-skill

annual_skill_by_model |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = AUC, decimals = 3) |>
  gt::fmt_scientific(columns = `p-value`, decimals = 2) |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "State x calendar-year onset AUC -- same methodology as covariate_summary.qmd's own single-covariate benchmark")
```

At this coarser, externally-benchmarked grain, the supervised model's own AUC (**`r round(sup_auc_annual, 3)`**, n = `r sup_n_onset_annual` onset / `r sup_n_no_annual` no-onset state-years) sits *below* both single covariates' own individually-validated AUCs (0.717 rain whiplash, 0.714 soil moisture whiplash, `covariate_summary.qmd`) -- not what a reader might expect from a model combining all four covariates plus zone effects. With only `r sup_n_onset_annual` onset examples feeding this specific test (a real, disclosed sample-size limit inherited from how few state-years `hmm_data` actually covers, not a flaw in the covariate-level tests), this is not a statistically confirmed difference either way (p = `r formatC(sup_p_annual, format = "e", digits = 2)`) -- but it's a genuine, honest finding worth flagging rather than assuming the more complex model must dominate a simpler, already-validated one. The comparison also *reverses* at this grain: the unsupervised model actually scores marginally higher here (AUC = `r round(unsup_auc_annual, 3)`) than the supervised one, the opposite of the paddock-season result above -- suggesting the annual-max aggregation this test needs (to stay comparable with the covariate-level benchmark) may itself be too coarse to capture what anchoring actually buys (paddock/zone-specific calibration, [Zone-specific deviations]), rather than anchoring providing no real value at the grain the model actually operates at.

### Hindcast against recorded plague years

```{r}
#| label: hindcast-scores

## Both models' scores, for the state-mean summary (the 90th-percentile summary gives similar
## results, see plague_hindcast_scores_*). Each model's pre-2013 hindcast is out-of-sample; from 2013
## the flags are in-sample for the supervised model (anchored) but still held out for the unsupervised one.
hindcast_scores <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(plague_hindcast_scores_supervised$scores, Model = "Supervised"),
  dplyr::mutate(plague_hindcast_scores_unsupervised$scores, Model = "Unsupervised")
) |>
  dplyr::filter(stat == "mean") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Predictor = dplyr::recode(predictor, occupancy = "Occupancy", onset = "Onset (same year)",
                              onset_lead = "Onset (previous year)", rain_whiplash = "Rain whiplash alone"),
    Era = dplyr::recode(era, hindcast = "Before 2013 (hindcast)", `anchored era` = "2013 on (anchored era)"),
    Era = factor(Era, levels = c("Before 2013 (hindcast)", "2013 on (anchored era)"))
  )

## The first hindcast season, for the text below.
hindcast_first <- plague_hindcast_supervised |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(onset)) |>
  dplyr::distinct(period, year_adj, season) |>
  dplyr::arrange(year_adj, match(season, c("Summer", "Autumn", "Winter", "Spring"))) |>
  dplyr::slice(1)
hindcast_first_label <- paste(hindcast_first$season, hindcast_first$year_adj)

## Numbers quoted in the text below.
get_hindcast <- function(model, predictor_name, era_name, col) {
  hindcast_scores[[col]][hindcast_scores$Model == model & hindcast_scores$predictor == predictor_name & hindcast_scores$era == era_name]
}
hindcast_n <- get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset", "hindcast", "n")
hindcast_n_flagged <- get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset", "hindcast", "n_flagged")
anchored_n <- get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset", "anchored era", "n")
anchored_n_flagged <- get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset", "anchored era", "n_flagged")
```

Plague anchors start in Summer 2013, and before 2013 there are almost no surveys (none in 2010-2011), so the plague years recorded in `yearly_plague_occurrence.csv` before 2013 are labels the model never saw. The hindcast (`r/d_hindcast_plague_occurrence.R`) runs the transition model over every 0.1 degree grain-zone cell from `r hindcast_first_label` onwards. It gives two quantities per cell and season: **onset**, the risk map's Pr(not-plague → plague), and **occupancy**, Pr(plague), propagated from season to season through each season's transitions. These are averaged over each state's cells, and the highest season in each year is scored against that state-year's flag (`r/d_score_plague_hindcast.R`).


```{r}
#| label: tbl-hindcast-scores

## Rain whiplash is a covariate, identical for both models, so it is shown once.
hindcast_scores |>
  dplyr::filter(!(Model == "Unsupervised" & predictor == "rain_whiplash")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Model = ifelse(predictor == "rain_whiplash", "(covariate only)", Model),
                `Within-state AUC (95% interval)` = sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", auc_within, auc_within_lcl, auc_within_ucl),
                `Pooled AUC` = sprintf("%.2f", auc)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(Era, Predictor, Model) |>
  dplyr::select(Era, Predictor, Model, `Within-state AUC (95% interval)`, `Pooled AUC`) |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Era") |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em") |>
  gt::tab_header(title = "Hindcast skill against recorded plague state-years",
                 subtitle = "State-mean of each season, highest season per year; intervals resample whole years")
```

- **Within-state AUC is the main score.** It compares flagged and unflagged years of the same state only; the pooled AUC also compares across states, where each state's baseline risk differs (e.g. Queensland's summer-cropping zone) for reasons unrelated to plague years.
- **Before 2013** there are `r hindcast_n_flagged` flagged out of `r hindcast_n` state-years. Same-year onset scores `r sprintf("%.2f", get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset", "hindcast", "auc_within"))` (supervised) and `r sprintf("%.2f", get_hindcast("Unsupervised", "onset", "hindcast", "auc_within"))` (unsupervised), against `r sprintf("%.2f", get_hindcast("Supervised", "rain_whiplash", "hindcast", "auc_within"))` for rain whiplash alone. The one-year-ahead onset scores `r sprintf("%.2f", get_hindcast("Supervised", "onset_lead", "hindcast", "auc_within"))` and `r sprintf("%.2f", get_hindcast("Unsupervised", "onset_lead", "hindcast", "auc_within"))`.
- **From 2013** only `r anchored_n_flagged` of `r anchored_n` state-years are flagged, so the intervals are too wide to separate the models. The unsupervised model's scores here are still out-of-sample.
- **Caveats.** The flags are coarse (a whole state, a whole calendar year, no WA). Rain whiplash's definition was chosen partly by checking it against these same flags (`r/b_compute_whiplash_raster.R`), so its score, and the models' use of it, are not fully blind. Occupancy is a per-paddock probability rather than the probability a plague is recorded somewhere in a state, so its Brier score (in `plague_hindcast_scores_*`) is only a coarse check.

```{r}
#| label: fig-hindcast-timeseries
#| fig-cap: "State-mean onset risk (highest season per year) from each model, with recorded plague years shaded. Dashed line: start of plague anchoring (2013)."
#| fig-height: 7

hindcast_series <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::mutate(plague_hindcast_scores_supervised$state_year, Model = "Supervised"),
  dplyr::mutate(plague_hindcast_scores_unsupervised$state_year, Model = "Unsupervised")
)
flagged_years <- dplyr::distinct(dplyr::filter(hindcast_series, flag == 1), state, year_adj)

ggplot(hindcast_series, aes(year_adj, onset_mean, colour = Model)) +
  geom_rect(data = flagged_years, aes(xmin = year_adj - 0.5, xmax = year_adj + 0.5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
            inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey80", alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2012.5, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(size = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ state, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Pr(not-plague → plague), state mean", colour = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

```{r}
#| label: mutze-1984

## Mutze (1989) mapped one SA plague extent within the covariate record (1984). Cell-level check:
## do SA cells inside the mapped extent get higher 1984 onset/occupancy than SA cells outside it?
mutze_1984 <- sf::st_union(sf::st_make_valid(dplyr::filter(mutze_plague_maps, year == 1984)))
sa_outline <- dplyr::filter(aus_shp, ST_NAME == "SA")
mutze_check <- purrr::imap_dfr(list(Supervised = plague_hindcast_supervised, Unsupervised = plague_hindcast_unsupervised), function(h, model) {
  cells_1984 <- h |>
    dplyr::filter(year_adj == 1984, !is.na(onset)) |>
    dplyr::group_by(cell, x, y) |>
    dplyr::summarise(onset = max(onset), occupancy = max(occupancy), .groups = "drop")
  if (nrow(cells_1984) == 0) return(tibble::tibble())
  pts <- sf::st_as_sf(cells_1984, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = sf::st_crs(aus_shp))
  in_sa <- lengths(sf::st_intersects(pts, sa_outline)) > 0
  inside <- lengths(sf::st_intersects(pts, sf::st_transform(mutze_1984, sf::st_crs(pts)))) > 0
  d <- cells_1984[in_sa, ]
  d$inside <- inside[in_sa]
  tibble::tibble(Model = model, `Cells inside` = sum(d$inside), `Cells outside` = sum(!d$inside),
                 `Onset inside` = mean(d$onset[d$inside]), `Onset outside` = mean(d$onset[!d$inside]),
                 `Onset AUC` = hindcast_auc(d$onset, as.integer(d$inside)),
                 `Occupancy AUC` = hindcast_auc(d$occupancy, as.integer(d$inside)))
})

## Sentence for the text below (inline code can't hold the backticked column names).
mutze_text <- if (nrow(mutze_check) > 0) {
  paste0("**Mutze's 1984 SA extent.** ", mutze_check[["Cells inside"]][1],
         " SA grain cells fall inside Mutze's (1989) mapped 1984 plague extent. Their 1984 onset risk averages ",
         sprintf("%.3f", mutze_check[["Onset inside"]][1]), " against ", sprintf("%.3f", mutze_check[["Onset outside"]][1]),
         " for the other SA cells (supervised); the cell-level AUC for inside vs outside is ",
         sprintf("%.2f", mutze_check[["Onset AUC"]][1]), " (supervised) and ", sprintf("%.2f", mutze_check[["Onset AUC"]][2]),
         " (unsupervised). This is a single mapped extent, so it is a spot check rather than a skill score.")
} else {
  "**Mutze's 1984 SA extent** falls before the first hindcast season, so it can't be checked."
}
```

`r mutze_text`


## Prediction: current risk map

```{r}
#| label: forecast-period

## The transition formula relates THIS season's covariates to the FOLLOWING season's state, and
## all four transition covariates are built entirely from realised (observed) data, no forward-
## looking forecast component in any of them, so none can ever be more current than the most
## recently completed month of real data. The model therefore only ever forecasts ONE season ahead
## of whatever the latest SHARED covariate period is -- rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak/
## min_temp_raster_coarse are monthly grain but gpp_rolling_raster_6/soil_moisture_raster_coarse
## are season-end-month grain only, so the shared period has to be found the same way
## predict_plague_risk() itself does, computed live here so this can't drift out of sync with the
## raster actually being predicted from.
```
