```{r}
shared_periods <- Reduce(intersect, list(names(rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak), names(gpp_rolling_raster_6), names(soil_moisture_raster_coarse), names(min_temp_raster_coarse)))
shared_month <- as.integer(sub("_.*", "", shared_periods))
shared_year  <- as.integer(sub(".*_", "", shared_periods))
predict_period <- shared_periods[order(shared_year, shared_month)][length(shared_periods)]
predict_month <- as.integer(sub("_.*", "", predict_period))
predict_year  <- as.integer(sub(".*_", "", predict_period))
covariate_season_info <- season_info(as.Date(paste(predict_year, predict_month, "15", sep = "-")))
covariate_season <- as.character(covariate_season_info$season)
covariate_year_adj <- covariate_season_info$year_adj

season_order <- c("Summer", "Autumn", "Winter", "Spring")
cur_idx <- match(covariate_season, season_order)
target_season <- season_order[(cur_idx %% 4) + 1]
target_year_adj <- if (target_season == "Summer") covariate_year_adj + 1 else covariate_year_adj

## Lead-time framing (2026-09, following a forecasting-literature review) -- translates the
## structural one-season-ahead limit above into the actual decision calendar CLAUDE.md's own
## stated purpose cares about (helping farmers decide when to bait), rather than leaving "one
## season ahead" as an abstract number with no obvious practical meaning. Grounded in standard,
## general Australian grain-cropping timing (winter cereals/canola sown roughly April-June; summer
## crops -- sorghum, cotton, maize -- sown roughly September-December, in the one zone this
## project's own summer_zone_ne distinguishes as having genuine summer cropping, r/d_build_hmm_
## data.R) -- ordinary agronomic knowledge, not a date sourced from this project's own data the way
## every other specific claim in this report is, so worded as indicative timing rather than a
## precise, per-season guarantee (real sowing/harvest dates vary by property, year and latitude
## within the fitted footprint).
lead_time_note <- switch(target_season,
  "Autumn" = "lands right in the window winter cereal/canola paddocks -- most of this model's own fitted footprint -- are typically sown in, a genuinely pre-sowing warning, timed while a bait decision can still change what goes into the ground",
  "Spring" = "lands right in the window summer crops are typically sown in the one zone with genuine summer cropping this model fits (\"NSW NE Qld SE\") -- a pre-sowing warning there too, though most of the rest of the fitted footprint is winter-only and already mid-way through this season's sown crop",
  "Winter" = "lands mid-way through an already-sown winter crop across most of the fitted footprint -- past the sowing decision, but still ahead of the flowering/grain-fill period baiting most needs to protect",
  "Summer" = "lands mid-way through an already-sown summer crop in the one zone with genuine summer cropping, and in the post-harvest stubble/fallow period for winter-only paddocks elsewhere -- past this season's own sowing decision everywhere in the fitted footprint"
)

risk_map_caption <- paste0(
  "Pr(not-plague -> plague) at every 0.1 degree cell within the fitted zones, using ",
  covariate_season, "-", covariate_year_adj,
  "'s rainfall whiplash, 6-month GPP, soil moisture and minimum temperature values to predict the transition into ",
  target_season, "-", target_year_adj,
  " -- one season ahead, the model's structural forecast limit (see below). Left: supervised (anchored) model. Right: unsupervised model, discovering its own state split with no anchors at all. Same colour scale/limits for both, so the two are directly comparable. Masked to the fitted zones only. ",
  "Colour scale is square-root transformed, not linear -- these risk values are heavily right-skewed (most cells low risk, a long tail toward high risk), so a plain linear scale leaves most of the map reading as flat green (see prose below the map for the numbers)."
)
```

### Predictor values at the current season

```{r}
#| label: fig-predictor-maps
#| fig-cap: !expr predictor_maps_caption
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-asp: 0.75

## The 3 headline transition covariates (min_temp omitted -- not requested here, and see
## [Known limitations] for its own untested-hypothesis caveat alongside soil_moisture's), each
## at the same predict_period computed above -- exactly the values fig-risk-map's own $predict()
## call below reads. One patchwork panel per covariate, stacked (not facet_wrap) since each has
## a very different unit/range (rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak spans negative, the other two don't)
## and needs its own colour scale -- a single shared scale would wash out whichever covariate has
## the smaller range. fit_zones_ll/zones_bbox/aus_sf reused from fig-spatial-key-years/setup
## above, not rebuilt here. terra::mask() to the fitted AE zone polygons -- same treatment
## fig-risk-map's own risk maps already get (r/d_predict_plague_risk.R) -- so cells outside
## the fitted zones (deserts, alps, cities, un-monitored zones) don't show a value at all, rather
## than implying a prediction-relevant covariate reading somewhere the model was never fit. Masked
## as the FULL multi-layer stack (not just the one predict_period layer) since the fixed colour
## limits below are computed from this same masked stack.
predictor_stacks <- list(
  `Rainfall whiplash`     = rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak,
  `GPP (6-month rolling)` = gpp_rolling_raster_6,
  `Soil moisture`         = soil_moisture_raster_coarse
) |>
  lapply(terra::mask, mask = terra::vect(fit_zones_ll))

predictor_rasters <- lapply(predictor_stacks, `[[`, predict_period)

## Colour limits fixed to each covariate's own FULL history (every season/year on record, not
## just predict_period) -- so a given value always reads as the same colour across report
## re-renders/seasons, rather than each render auto-rescaling to whatever period happens to be
## current. terra::global(..., "range") is cheap even across a 500+ layer stack (~1s, confirmed
## live) -- no need to cache/precompute outside this chunk.
predictor_limits <- lapply(predictor_stacks, function(s) {
  rng <- terra::global(s, "range", na.rm = TRUE)
  c(min(rng$min, na.rm = TRUE), max(rng$max, na.rm = TRUE))
})

predictor_maps_caption <- paste0(
  "The 3 covariates driving the transition probabilities, at ", covariate_season, "-", covariate_year_adj,
  " (", predict_period, ") -- the same period the risk map below is predicted from. Left to right: the raw grid, its AE zone mean, its GRDC growing-subregion mean (a finer grain, clipped to the fitted zones' own footprint). Colour scales are fixed to each covariate's own full 1982+ record (not just this period), so colour is comparable across re-renders. Grey lines are the fitted AE zone borders."
)

## rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak is a z-score-like anomaly sweep, genuinely centred on 0 (a
## negative value is a real "wetter-getting-drier" signal, not just noise near a floor) -- white
## needs to sit exactly AT 0, ruling out scale_fill_distiller() (tried first, centres its middle
## colour on the midpoint of whatever LIMITS spans, not on 0). scale_fill_gradient2() (tried
## second) gets 0 right but has its own bug for this specific asymmetric range (-1.6 to 4.3):
## its rescale_mid() stretches the colour scale SYMMETRICALLY around the midpoint using the
## LARGER of the two distances (here 4.3), so the shorter (negative) side never reaches full
## colour intensity -- confirmed live, this is exactly why the blue end looked washed out/
## "transparent" next to the fully-saturated red end, not an actual alpha/transparency setting
## anywhere in this code. Fixed with scale_fill_gradientn()'s own `values` argument instead --
## an explicit stop position for white at 0's own true fractional location within the real
## (asymmetric) limits, computed live via scales::rescale() so it stays correct if the
## full-history range itself shifts on a future re-render -- both ends now reach full colour
## saturation at their own true data extreme. gpp_rolling6 and soil_moisture are both plain
## continuous, always-positive covariates with no such reference point (unaffected by any of
## this), so they share one viridis gradient -- a consistent "low = dark purple, high = yellow"
## reading across both, rather than each getting its own unrelated hue (Greens vs. Blues, tried
## first) that implies a difference in kind that isn't really there. guide_colorbar()'s own
## title.position = "top" puts each legend's title above its bar rather than ggplot's own
## default of squeezed to the left -- confirmed live this also fixes a real overlap bug: the
## left-aligned title's own box height wasn't reserved consistently once these panels got narrower
## (3 columns, below), so the title text crept up into the map above it in some panels.
rain_whiplash_limits <- predictor_limits[["Rainfall whiplash"]]
rain_whiplash_zero_stop <- scales::rescale(0, from = rain_whiplash_limits) # 0's own fractional position within the (asymmetric) limits
predictor_guide <- guide_colorbar(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5)
predictor_palettes <- list(
  `Rainfall whiplash`     = function(p) p + scale_fill_gradientn(colors = c("#2166AC", "white", "#B2182B"), values = c(0, rain_whiplash_zero_stop, 1), limits = rain_whiplash_limits, name = "Rainfall whiplash (z-score)", guide = predictor_guide),
  `GPP (6-month rolling)` = function(p) p + scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = predictor_limits[["GPP (6-month rolling)"]], name = "GPP (gC/m²/day)", guide = predictor_guide),
  `Soil moisture`         = function(p) p + scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = predictor_limits[["Soil moisture"]], name = "Soil moisture (%)", labels = scales::percent, guide = predictor_guide)
)

## Zone-mean/subregion-mean versions (2nd/3rd columns below) -- one value per polygon
## (terra::extract()'s own zonal mean, not a per-cell operation, so this is cheap even for the
## 29 subregions -- confirmed live ~0.5s), on the SAME colour scale/limits as the raw map (1st
## column) for a direct read of how much detail each level of aggregation throws away.
## grdc_subregion_ll is already clipped to the fitted zones' own footprint (fig-spatial-key-years
## above) -- no further filtering needed here.
predictor_zone_sf <- purrr::imap(predictor_rasters, function(r, label) {
  zone_mean <- terra::extract(r, terra::vect(fit_zones_ll), fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE, ID = FALSE)[[1]]
  dplyr::mutate(fit_zones_ll, value = zone_mean)
})
predictor_subregion_sf <- purrr::imap(predictor_rasters, function(r, label) {
  subregion_mean <- terra::extract(r, terra::vect(grdc_subregion_ll), fun = mean, na.rm = TRUE, ID = FALSE)[[1]]
  dplyr::mutate(grdc_subregion_ll, value = subregion_mean) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(value)) # subregions with no real overlap with the masked raster at all
})

base_map_theme <- theme_void(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(0.8, "cm"), legend.key.height = unit(0.3, "cm"),
        legend.title = element_text(size = 9), legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 10.5, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

predictor_maps <- purrr::imap(predictor_rasters, function(r, label) {
  df <- as.data.frame(r, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  names(df)[3] <- "value"

  raw_map <- ggplot() +
    geom_tile(data = df, aes(x, y, fill = value)) +
    geom_sf(data = fit_zones_ll, fill = NA, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_sf(data = aus_sf, fill = NA, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.6) +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(zones_bbox["xmin"], zones_bbox["xmax"]),
             ylim = c(zones_bbox["ymin"], zones_bbox["ymax"]), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = label) +
    base_map_theme

  zone_map <- ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = predictor_zone_sf[[label]], aes(fill = value), colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_sf(data = aus_sf, fill = NA, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.6) +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(zones_bbox["xmin"], zones_bbox["xmax"]),
             ylim = c(zones_bbox["ymin"], zones_bbox["ymax"]), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = paste(label, "– AE zone mean")) +
    base_map_theme

  subregion_map <- ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = predictor_subregion_sf[[label]], aes(fill = value), colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.15) +
    geom_sf(data = aus_sf, fill = NA, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.6) +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(zones_bbox["xmin"], zones_bbox["xmax"]),
             ylim = c(zones_bbox["ymin"], zones_bbox["ymax"]), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = paste(label, "– GRDC subregion mean")) +
    base_map_theme

  ## Three elements per covariate (raw, zone mean, subregion mean), not one -- purrr::flatten()
  ## below unnests this one level so wrap_plots(ncol = 3) fills each triple row-by-row, one
  ## row/covariate.
  list(predictor_palettes[[label]](raw_map), predictor_palettes[[label]](zone_map), predictor_palettes[[label]](subregion_map))
})

patchwork::wrap_plots(purrr::flatten(predictor_maps), ncol = 3)
```

Left to right: the raw grid, its AE-zone mean, its GRDC-subregion mean (roughly 4x finer-grained than AE zone) -- same colour scale across all three so the loss of detail at each level of aggregation is directly comparable, masked to the fitted AE zones' own footprint throughout, same as the risk map below. `rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak` shows the clearest regional structure this season, with the elevated (red) band in South Australia's mid-north visible against the calmer (blue) NSW zones -- coarse enough on its own that even the AE-zone mean keeps most of that signal; `soil_moisture` and `gpp_rolling6` vary more gradually across the fitted region, so aggregating either loses more genuine within-zone/within-subregion variation.

```{r}
#| label: fig-risk-map
#| fig-cap: !expr risk_map_caption
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-asp: 0.4

## Side by side, one panel per model_variants entry (setup chunk) -- both models' own risk maps
## are real, cached _targets.R targets (tar_map() over model variant), not derived from one
## another, so this is a genuine comparison, not a duplicate view. risk_df_by_model keeps every
## model's own data frame (not just the combined plot) since risk-stats below needs each one
## separately.
risk_df_by_model <- purrr::imap(model_variants, function(m, label) {
  df <- as.data.frame(m$risk_map, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  names(df)[3] <- "risk"
  df
})
pad <- 0.6
xr <- range(risk_df_by_model[[1]]$x); yr <- range(risk_df_by_model[[1]]$y) # same fit_zones_sf mask for both models, so either's own extent works

## Genuinely right-skewed (confirmed live: median 7%, 90th percentile 37%, max 98%) -- a plain
## linear 0-1 colour scale spends almost its entire visual range on the rare >90% tail, so the
## ecologically real, actionable structure sitting in the 20-70% band (most of NSW, this season)
## reads as flat, undifferentiated green, masking exactly the signal a farmer deciding whether to
## bait most needs to see. trans = "sqrt" fixes this WITHOUT changing the underlying data, limits,
## or losing any information at the top (max 0.98 still reads as essentially full red) -- it just
## redistributes visual colour-space toward the low/mid range where the actual data lives.
## Confirmed live as a real, substantial difference, not a marginal tweak -- see this report's own
## revision history/commit for a side-by-side. breaks chosen to read naturally on a sqrt axis
## (roughly even spacing after the transform, not raw 0/25/50/75/100). One shared scale/limits
## across both panels (not each auto-scaling to its own model's own range) so colour is directly
## comparable model to model, not just within one.
risk_maps <- purrr::imap(risk_df_by_model, function(df, label) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_tile(data = df, aes(x, y, fill = risk), width = 0.1, height = 0.1) +
    geom_sf(data = aus_sf, fill = NA, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(colors = hazard_colors, limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent,
                          breaks = c(0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 1), trans = "sqrt",
                          name = "Plague transition risk") +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(xr[1]-pad, xr[2]+pad), ylim = c(yr[1]-pad, yr[2]+pad), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = label) +
    theme_void(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(1.6, "cm"),
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))
})

patchwork::wrap_plots(risk_maps, ncol = 2, guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

**This map predicts risk for `r target_season`-`r target_year_adj`**, using `r covariate_season`-`r covariate_year_adj`'s own covariate values (the most recent period shared by all four, `r predict_period`). One season ahead is the structural limit of the current design -- all four transition covariates are built purely from realised observations, so none can be computed past the most recently completed month of real data, and the transition formula always relates one season's covariates to the *following* season's state. Forecasting further out would require forecasting the covariates themselves, which this model doesn't do.

In practical terms, that one-season structural limit isn't a fixed amount of lead time against the farming calendar it's meant to inform -- it depends on which season the forecast happens to land on. This particular `r target_season` forecast `r lead_time_note`. (General agronomic timing, not sourced from this project's own data -- offered as context for reading the map, not a claim this report can verify the way its other numbers are.)

```{r}
#| label: risk-stats

## median converted to a percentage too (100*), matching pct_gt50/pct_gt20 -- a real bug caught
## live on the real render (2026-09): the raw proportion was slipping through unconverted
## (rounding e.g. 0.071 to "0.1") while the column header already said "Median risk (%)".
risk_stats_by_model <- purrr::imap_dfr(risk_df_by_model, function(df, label) {
  df |> summarise(Model = label, median = 100*median(risk), pct_gt50 = 100*mean(risk > 0.5), pct_gt20 = 100*mean(risk > 0.2), n = n())
})
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-risk-stats

risk_stats_by_model |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c(median, pct_gt50, pct_gt20), decimals = 1) |>
  gt::cols_label(median = "Median risk (%)", pct_gt50 = "Cells > 50% risk", pct_gt20 = "Cells > 20% risk", n = "Valid cells") |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "0.85em")
```

The highest-risk band runs along South Australia's western coastline near the Eyre Peninsula, with a smaller hotspot in central-east New South Wales, for both models (though the unsupervised model's own numbers should stay stable as the anchoring pipeline's own upstream data is mid-rebuild, unlike the supervised model's -- see [Overview]). Masked to the `r n_distinct(hmm_data$ae_zone)` fitted zones only -- nothing is extrapolated beyond those, e.g. to `"Qld Central"` or any other untrained zone (WA's own 4 zones joined the fit itself 2026-09, so are no longer a blanket exclusion here -- see [Data and anchoring]). The colour scale above is square-root transformed (not linear), since both models' own risk values are heavily right-skewed -- a plain linear scale would leave most of the map reading as flat, uninformative green, masking real structure in the 20-50% band that matters for an early-warning use case.

### Translating risk into an operational threshold

The map above reports Pr(entering plague) as a raw percentage. CLAUDE.md's own stated purpose is more specific than that: giving farmers useful early warning of *moderate-high or increasing* mouse activity so they can decide when to bait -- the same kind of categorical language recent_plague_maps' own severity field (minor/moderate/severe) and MouseAlert both already use. This section calibrates one concrete cutoff on the model's own probability scale against that same real anchor data (2026-09, following the same literature review as [Full-model onset skill] above), rather than leaving every reader to guess what a given percentage means operationally.

```{r}
#| label: operational-threshold

## Youden's J statistic (sensitivity + specificity - 1, maximised over every observed threshold) is
## the standard, textbook way to pick one operating point from a continuous predictor against a
## known binary outcome -- used here as-is, not a project-specific invention. Supervised model only
## -- matching every other supervised-only section built on this same evidentiary standard ([Zone-
## specific deviations], [Validation against known history]) -- since [Full-model onset skill]
## above already shows the unsupervised model's own predicted Pr(enter) doesn't discriminate real
## onsets at all (in fact runs slightly backwards), so a threshold calibrated against it would be
## meaningless. Reuses eligible_by_model$Supervised (onset-skill-data, above) directly rather than
## recomputing the same $predict() call a second time.
supervised_eligible <- eligible_by_model$Supervised
threshold_candidates <- sort(unique(supervised_eligible$p_enter))
roc_points <- purrr::map_dfr(threshold_candidates, function(th) {
  predicted_high <- supervised_eligible$p_enter >= th
  actual_onset   <- supervised_eligible$next_state == 2
  tibble::tibble(
    threshold   = th,
    sensitivity = mean(predicted_high[actual_onset]),
    specificity = mean(!predicted_high[!actual_onset])
  )
})
best_threshold <- roc_points |>
  dplyr::mutate(youden = sensitivity + specificity - 1) |>
  dplyr::slice_max(youden, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)

## What fraction of THIS season's own risk map (fig-risk-map above) already sits at or above that
## cutoff -- ties the abstract threshold back to the actual current map, not just the historical
## calibration sample.
pct_current_map_above <- 100 * mean(risk_df_by_model$Supervised$risk >= best_threshold$threshold)
```

A risk cutoff of **`r scales::percent(best_threshold$threshold, accuracy = 0.1)`** best separates real onsets from real non-onsets in the paddock-season anchor data above (Youden's J = `r round(best_threshold$youden, 2)`), catching **`r scales::percent(best_threshold$sensitivity, accuracy = 1)`** of real onsets while correctly clearing **`r scales::percent(best_threshold$specificity, accuracy = 1)`** of seasons that stayed clear. Read this as roughly where a MouseAlert-style "Moderate-High" reading sits on this model's own probability scale, not a precise operational rule -- the underlying calibration sample (`r nrow(supervised_eligible)` eligible paddock-seasons, `r sum(supervised_eligible$next_state == 2)` real onsets) is still thin, the same small-N caveat [Data and anchoring] and [Full-model onset skill] both already carry. **`r round(pct_current_map_above, 1)`%** of this season's own risk map (@fig-risk-map) already sits at or above that cutoff.

### Nowcast: latest available covariates

```{r}
#| label: forecast-period-nowcast

## Same shared-period logic as the forecast-period chunk above, but over the nowcast rasters
## (gpp_rolling_raster_6_nowcast/soil_moisture_raster_coarse_nowcast in place of their season-end-
## trimmed namesakes -- rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak/min_temp_raster_coarse are unchanged, already
## full monthly grain) -- see _targets.R's own plague_risk_map_nowcast comment and
## r/d_predict_plague_risk.R's header for why this can land on a later period than the main map
## above: it isn't held back to the next Feb/May/Aug/Nov boundary.
shared_periods_nowcast <- Reduce(intersect, list(names(rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak), names(gpp_rolling_raster_6_nowcast), names(soil_moisture_raster_coarse_nowcast), names(min_temp_raster_coarse)))
shared_month_nowcast <- as.integer(sub("_.*", "", shared_periods_nowcast))
shared_year_nowcast  <- as.integer(sub(".*_", "", shared_periods_nowcast))
predict_period_nowcast <- shared_periods_nowcast[order(shared_year_nowcast, shared_month_nowcast)][length(shared_periods_nowcast)]
predict_month_nowcast <- as.integer(sub("_.*", "", predict_period_nowcast))
predict_year_nowcast  <- as.integer(sub(".*_", "", predict_period_nowcast))
covariate_season_info_nowcast <- season_info(as.Date(paste(predict_year_nowcast, predict_month_nowcast, "15", sep = "-")))
covariate_season_nowcast <- as.character(covariate_season_info_nowcast$season)
covariate_year_adj_nowcast <- covariate_season_info_nowcast$year_adj

cur_idx_nowcast <- match(covariate_season_nowcast, season_order)
target_season_nowcast <- season_order[(cur_idx_nowcast %% 4) + 1]
target_year_adj_nowcast <- if (target_season_nowcast == "Summer") covariate_year_adj_nowcast + 1 else covariate_year_adj_nowcast

risk_map_nowcast_caption <- paste0(
  "Pr(not-plague -> plague) at every 0.1 degree cell within the fitted zones, using ",
  covariate_season_nowcast, "-", covariate_year_adj_nowcast,
  "'s rainfall whiplash, 6-month GPP, soil moisture and minimum temperature values to predict the transition into ",
  target_season_nowcast, "-", target_year_adj_nowcast,
  " -- same model and covariates as the map above, but read off the latest complete calendar month (",
  predict_period_nowcast, ") rather than the last season-end boundary (", predict_period, "), so this map is current even mid-season. No uncertainty variant yet (see prose below)."
)
```

The map above updates only at the Feb/May/Aug/Nov season boundary, because `gpp_rolling6`/`soil_moisture` are season-end-aligned covariates -- so for part of every season it is necessarily predicting off the *previous* season's covariates. This nowcast map instead uses the latest complete calendar month for every covariate (`r predict_period_nowcast` here, vs. `r predict_period` above), so it can move from `r covariate_season`-`r covariate_year_adj` to `r covariate_season_nowcast`-`r covariate_year_adj_nowcast` as soon as real data allows, rather than waiting for the next season-end. It is still 100% real, complete-month data -- no partial-month averaging, no trend extrapolation -- just a relaxed alignment requirement (see `_targets.R`'s own `plague_risk_map_nowcast` comment and r/d_predict_plague_risk.R's header). Added 2026-09 to unblock a real Spring-2026 request; no posterior-uncertainty variant exists for it yet (deliberately deferred, not an oversight -- see the TO-DO note at the top of `_targets.R`), so treat this map as a point estimate only, without the [Prediction uncertainty] section's own confidence bands.

### Prediction uncertainty

```{r}
#| label: fig-risk-map-uncertainty
#| fig-cap: !expr risk_uncertainty_caption
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-asp: 0.4

## Uncertainty on the RAW PROBABILITY scale (ucl - lcl) is a misleading measure here -- confirmed
## live (2026-08): it's compressed by the logit link whenever the point estimate itself sits near
## 0 or 1, so the far-west SA cluster driving the supervised model's own most extreme risk values
## (see [Known limitations]) -- exactly the cells with the least real evidence behind them --
## shows a deceptively NARROW probability-scale CI (0.09) despite a genuinely enormous LOGIT-scale
## CI (3.16, the widest of any cell in the whole grid). Plotting logit(ucl) - logit(lcl) instead
## reveals this correctly -- direct visual confirmation of the [Known limitations] finding, not
## just a caveat in prose. Purple palette (not hazard_colors or viridis) deliberately -- this is a
## different KIND of quantity (confidence, not risk itself or a raw covariate), so it gets its own
## visual identity rather than implying it's directly comparable to either. See
## plague_risk_map_uncertainty_* (_targets.R, r/d_predict_plague_risk.R) for how mle/lcl/ucl are
## computed -- 500 posterior draws of each model's own fixed+random-effect coefficients, the same
## mechanism this report's own [Covariate effects on transition probability] curves already use.
##
## Side by side, same pattern as fig-risk-map above -- both models' own uncertainty is a real,
## separately-computed quantity, not derived from one another. risk_df/uncertainty_df (singular,
## the supervised model's own version) kept below for the two trial figures further down, which
## stay single-model -- see their own comments for why.
.logit <- function(p) log(p / (1 - p))
uncertainty_df_by_model <- purrr::imap(model_variants, function(m, label) {
  rast_width <- .logit(m$risk_map_uncertainty[["ucl"]]) - .logit(m$risk_map_uncertainty[["lcl"]])
  df <- as.data.frame(rast_width, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  names(df)[3] <- "logit_width"
  df
})
risk_df <- risk_df_by_model$Supervised
uncertainty_df <- uncertainty_df_by_model$Supervised

## One shared scale across both panels (not each auto-scaling to its own model's own range) so
## uncertainty is directly comparable model to model, matching the risk map's own treatment above.
uncertainty_shared_limits <- range(unlist(lapply(uncertainty_df_by_model, `[[`, "logit_width")))

risk_uncertainty_caption <- "95% CI width for the risk map above, on the logit (log-odds) scale, not the raw probability scale -- a probability-scale width looks small whenever the point estimate itself sits near 0% or 100%, regardless of how wide the underlying uncertainty really is, so it would hide exactly the cells most worth distrusting. Left/right match the risk map above. Same colour scale/limits for both panels. Same period/extent/mask as the risk map. Darker purple = wider CI = less certain."

uncertainty_maps <- purrr::imap(uncertainty_df_by_model, function(df, label) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_tile(data = df, aes(x, y, fill = logit_width), width = 0.1, height = 0.1) +
    geom_sf(data = aus_sf, fill = NA, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.6) +
    scale_fill_distiller(palette = "Purples", direction = 1, limits = uncertainty_shared_limits, name = "95% CI width (logit scale)") +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(xr[1]-pad, xr[2]+pad), ylim = c(yr[1]-pad, yr[2]+pad), expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = label) +
    theme_void(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(1.6, "cm"),
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))
})

patchwork::wrap_plots(uncertainty_maps, ncol = 2, guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r}
#| label: uncertainty-stats

## Supervised model only below (matching [Known limitations]'s own SA Vic Mallee finding, which is
## specific to the anchored model's own poorly-identified coefficient) -- the figure above shows
## both, but this specific numeric drill-down is about the supervised model's own known issue.
uncertainty_stats <- uncertainty_df |>
  summarise(median = median(logit_width), max = max(logit_width))
top_uncertain <- uncertainty_df |> slice_max(logit_width, n = 1)
top_risk_cell <- risk_df |> slice_max(risk, n = 1)
```

Supervised model: median 95% CI width across the grid: **`r round(uncertainty_stats$median, 2)`** logit units; the single widest is **`r round(uncertainty_stats$max, 2)`**, at (`r round(top_uncertain$x, 1)`, `r round(top_uncertain$y, 1)`) -- `r cell_distance <- round(sqrt((top_uncertain$x - top_risk_cell$x)^2 + (top_uncertain$y - top_risk_cell$y)^2), 2); if (cell_distance == 0) "the exact same cell as" else paste("within", cell_distance, "degrees of")` the risk map's own single highest-risk cell. That's not a coincidence: hmmTMB itself already flags this model's own posterior covariance as ill-conditioned (`Inversion of precision matrix... using 'MASS::ginv' instead`, this report's own render log) -- a further reason to treat the far-west SA cluster's extreme risk values as an open question, not a confirmed reading, until the [Known limitations] finding is resolved.

### Trial: risk and uncertainty in one map

```{r}
#| label: fig-risk-map-combined-trial
#| fig-cap: !expr risk_combined_caption

## TRIAL, not adopted -- kept alongside (not replacing) the two-panel risk/uncertainty maps
## above, per request, so the two approaches can be compared directly. Same risk raster/colour
## scale as the risk map, with alpha (transparency) additionally encoding confidence -- more
## transparent = wider (less certain) CI, so an over-confident-looking red cell with a bad CI
## fades rather than reading as solidly alarming.
##
## alpha mapped from logit_width's own RANK (percentile), not its raw value -- confirmed live the
## raw value has the exact same right-skew problem the risk colour scale itself had (median CI
## width 0.83 logit units, only the top handful of cells reach anywhere near the max of 3.16), so
## a plain linear rescale left >97% of cells within a narrow near-opaque alpha band and the fade
## effect was barely visible. Percentile rank spreads it out properly, same fix in spirit as the
## colour scale's own sqrt transform above. Floor of 0.15 (not 0) so no cell disappears entirely
## -- it's still a real prediction, just a low-confidence one. scale_alpha_identity() (no legend)
## since a continuous fill legend AND a continuous alpha legend together read as cluttered for a
## trial figure -- the caption explains the encoding instead. grey40 plot background (not white)
## so faded cells are visibly faded rather than blending into a white page.
##
## Real reservation, stated plainly rather than glossed over: risk and uncertainty are strongly
## correlated in this specific dataset (r = 0.84 on the raw probability scale) -- confirmed live
## -- so colour and alpha move together more than a clean bivariate encoding really wants. That
## makes it genuinely harder to tell "muted because uncertain" apart from "just less risky" than
## the two separate panels above manage. This isn't a fixable choice-of-statistic problem, checked
## live using hmmTMB's own return_post = TRUE (raw posterior draws, not just mle/lcl/ucl): the
## posterior SD on the SAME (probability) scale correlates with risk just as strongly (r = 0.91,
## essentially identical to CI width, as expected -- they're both just summaries of the same
## spread) and even the logit-scale SD -- a genuinely different scale -- only softens it to
## r = 0.71/0.60. The correlation is real and substantive: the SAME poorly-identified
## `SA Vic Mallee` zone slope ([Known limitations]) drives both the extreme point estimate AND the
## wide uncertainty together, by construction, not an artefact of measuring "width" specifically.
## See the distance-based trial below for an alpha channel that turned out to be much less
## entangled with risk. Not a reason to rule this one out, but a real trade-off to weigh before
## adopting it over the clearer (if less compact) two-panel version.
##
## Supervised model only -- both trial figures stayed single-model when the risk/uncertainty maps
## above became a dual-model comparison (2026-08): they're both explicitly experimental, and
## doubling an unadopted technique to 4 panels traded clarity for a comparison nobody's asked for
## yet. model_variants$Supervised (setup chunk) is the one place this would need to change if that
## scope decision is ever revisited.
combined_df <- as.data.frame(c(model_variants$Supervised$risk_map, .logit(model_variants$Supervised$risk_map_uncertainty[["ucl"]]) - .logit(model_variants$Supervised$risk_map_uncertainty[["lcl"]])),
                              xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
names(combined_df) <- c("x", "y", "risk", "logit_width")
combined_df$confidence_alpha <- scales::rescale(-rank(combined_df$logit_width), to = c(0.15, 1))

risk_combined_caption <- "TRIAL -- same risk values as the map above, with transparency additionally encoding confidence (more transparent = wider, less certain CI, ranked so the fade is visible across the full range, not just the extreme tail). Not adopted over the two-panel version above -- see the caveat in the code comments about risk and uncertainty being correlated in this dataset, which makes the two channels harder to read apart than they would be if independent."

ggplot() +
  geom_tile(data = combined_df, aes(x, y, fill = risk, alpha = confidence_alpha), width = 0.1, height = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(data = aus_sf, fill = NA, colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colors = hazard_colors, limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent,
                        breaks = c(0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 1), trans = "sqrt", name = "Plague transition risk\n(more transparent = less certain)") +
  scale_alpha_identity() +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(xr[1]-pad, xr[2]+pad), ylim = c(yr[1]-pad, yr[2]+pad), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(1.6, "cm"),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "grey40", colour = NA),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = "grey40", colour = NA),
        legend.text = element_text(colour = "white"), legend.title = element_text(colour = "white"))
```

### Trial: risk and distance-from-survey-data in one map

```{r}
#| label: fig-risk-map-distance-trial
#| fig-cap: !expr risk_distance_caption

## Second trial alpha channel, tried after the uncertainty one above turned out too entangled with
## risk to read cleanly (r = 0.84-0.91 confirmed live, see that trial's own caveat). This one
## targets the OTHER half of the [Known limitations] finding directly -- not "is this zone's own
## slope poorly identified" but "is this specific cell geographically far from any real paddock
## that trained it" -- a purely geometric quantity, computed independently of the fitted
## coefficients entirely, so there's no structural reason it should correlate with risk the way
## posterior spread did. Confirmed live: it doesn't (r = 0.065, essentially uncorrelated) -- a
## genuinely cleaner bivariate encoding than the uncertainty trial above.
##
## Distance is to the nearest survey paddock WITHIN THE SAME ae_zone as each cell, not the nearest
## paddock anywhere -- tried the simpler "nearest any paddock" version first and reverted it same
## session: it produced a real, backwards-looking artefact (confirmed live) where sparsely-sampled
## NSW zones (few paddocks spread across a huge area) faded MORE than the far-west SA cluster
## actually driving this report's own overconfidence finding, simply because some OTHER zone's
## paddock happened to sit geographically nearby -- a different zone's paddock is irrelevant here,
## since it trained a different zone's own coefficients entirely. Restricting to same-zone
## paddocks fixes this and, for the specific cluster this report is actually worried about,
## reproduces the exact 202km figure already documented in [Known limitations] -- not a
## coincidence, the same real gap measured two different ways.
##
## Implementation: one terra::distance() call per zone (fast -- confirmed live ~3-5s total for all
## 7 zones, unlike the uncertainty trial's 500-posterior-draw mechanism, so this is computed
## directly here rather than needing its own cached _targets.R target. Supervised model only, same
## scope decision as the uncertainty trial above -- see its own comment for why.
paddocks_by_zone <- hmm_data |>
  distinct(ID, longitude, latitude, ae_zone) |>
  filter(!is.na(longitude), !is.na(latitude))

zone_rast <- terra::rasterize(terra::vect(sf::st_transform(fit_zones_sf, terra::crs(model_variants$Supervised$risk_map))), model_variants$Supervised$risk_map[[1]], field = "ae_zone")
distance_cell_df <- as.data.frame(c(model_variants$Supervised$risk_map, zone_rast), xy = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE)
names(distance_cell_df) <- c("x", "y", "risk", "ae_zone")

zone_levels <- sort(unique(paddocks_by_zone$ae_zone))
dist_by_zone <- rast(lapply(zone_levels, function(z) {
  zone_pts <- terra::vect(dplyr::filter(paddocks_by_zone, ae_zone == z), geom = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = "EPSG:4326")
  terra::distance(model_variants$Supervised$risk_map[[1]], zone_pts, unit = "km")
}))
names(dist_by_zone) <- zone_levels
dist_by_zone_df <- as.data.frame(dist_by_zone, xy = TRUE, na.rm = FALSE)

distance_cell_df$dist_km <- NA_real_
for (z in zone_levels) {
  idx <- which(distance_cell_df$ae_zone == z)
  distance_cell_df$dist_km[idx] <- dist_by_zone_df[[z]][idx]
}
distance_cell_df <- dplyr::filter(distance_cell_df, !is.na(risk), !is.na(dist_km))

## Rank-based alpha again -- same reasoning as the uncertainty trial's own sqrt/rank fixes above,
## though this distance distribution is less pathologically skewed to begin with.
distance_cell_df$distance_alpha <- scales::rescale(-rank(distance_cell_df$dist_km), to = c(0.15, 1))

risk_distance_caption <- "TRIAL -- same risk values as the map above, with transparency instead encoding distance to the nearest real survey paddock WITHIN THE SAME AE zone (more transparent = further from any paddock that actually trained that zone's own coefficients). Unlike the uncertainty trial above, this channel is only weakly correlated with risk (r = 0.065, confirmed live) -- so it reads as a genuinely separate piece of information, not a re-statement of the colour scale wearing a different name."

ggplot() +
  geom_tile(data = distance_cell_df, aes(x, y, fill = risk, alpha = distance_alpha), width = 0.1, height = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(data = aus_sf, fill = NA, colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.25, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_gradientn(colors = hazard_colors, limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent,
                        breaks = c(0, 0.05, 0.2, 0.5, 1), trans = "sqrt", name = "Plague transition risk\n(more transparent = further from own-zone survey data)") +
  scale_alpha_identity() +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(xr[1]-pad, xr[2]+pad), ylim = c(yr[1]-pad, yr[2]+pad), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = unit(1.6, "cm"),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "grey40", colour = NA),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = "grey40", colour = NA),
        legend.text = element_text(colour = "white"), legend.title = element_text(colour = "white"))
```

Of the two trial encodings, this one seems the more promising candidate if a single combined map is wanted over the clearer two-panel version -- the alpha channel here carries real, largely independent information (spatial coverage) rather than substantially re-stating the colour channel (statistical confidence, itself driven by the same coefficients as risk). Still a trial, not adopted as the primary view; the two-panel risk/uncertainty maps above remain the clearest communication of the [Known limitations] finding on their own.

## Known limitations

Full investigation history for every item below -- what was tried, what failed and why -- lives in `r/d_fit_plague_hmm.R`'s and `r/c_anchor_plague_state.R`'s own headers, not repeated here.

```{r}
#| label: known-limitations-stats

## Live-computed from whiplash_zone_tbl ([Zone-specific deviations] above, already in scope by this
## point in the render), not transcribed -- a hardcoded figure here drifted out of sync with the
## live table on a real re-render once already (2026-09, confirmed live: table showed 2.353, this
## bullet still said 2.344 from when the finding was first written), exactly the staleness this
## project's own convention of computing numbers live elsewhere is meant to avoid. Since the
## 2026-09 move to a hierarchical (partially-pooled) zone slope, "Total slope" (pooled fixed effect
## + that zone's own random-effect deviation) is the modern equivalent of the old fixed-interaction
## spec's own per-zone coefficient -- see that section's header for the full mechanism. S1>S2 only
## (entering plague) -- the transition the risk map itself maps (Pr(not-plague -> plague)); S2>S1's
## own zone slopes are a different coefficient set entirely, not part of this finding.
mallee_slope <- whiplash_zone_tbl$`Total slope`[whiplash_zone_tbl$Transition == "S1>S2" & whiplash_zone_tbl$`AE zone` == "SA Vic Mallee"]
other_slopes <- whiplash_zone_tbl$`Total slope`[whiplash_zone_tbl$Transition == "S1>S2" & whiplash_zone_tbl$`AE zone` != "SA Vic Mallee"]

## burrow_count.mean's joint-precision near-singularity (found 2026-09 investigating a real
## solve()-failed warning from plague_risk_map_uncertainty_*'s own n_post = 500 posterior sampling,
## hmmTMB's HMM$predict() -> prec_to_cov() -> MASS::ginv() fallback path, r/utility.R). Condition
## number computed live from each fitted model's own TMB joint precision matrix -- not transcribed,
## same reasoning as mallee_slope above. Root cause: summer_zone_ne (r/d_build_hmm_data.R) is
## defined as exactly ae_zone == "NSW NE Qld SE", so burrow_count.mean's season:summer_zone_ne
## detection term and its own free-per-state ae_zone term are collinear for that one zone's rows --
## confirmed by eigen-decomposing jointPrecision and reading off the near-null eigenvector's
## loadings, which land almost entirely on burrow_count.mean's state1/state2 intercepts, its
## ae_zoneNSW NE Qld SE dummy, and all four season:summer_zone_ne levels.
cond_number_sup   <- { ev <- eigen(as.matrix(plague_hmm$tmb_rep()$jointPrecision), symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values; max(ev) / min(ev) }
cond_number_unsup <- { ev <- eigen(as.matrix(plague_hmm_unsupervised$tmb_rep()$jointPrecision), symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values; max(ev) / min(ev) }
```

- **The chew-card family depends on a patched hmmTMB** -- `betabinom` isn't in CRAN hmmTMB 1.1.2, so `renv.lock` pins github.com/matt-w-rees/hmmTMB (branch `betabinom-dev`: hmmTMB's development version plus the family). Upstream hmmTMB fixes only arrive if merged into that branch, until the family is accepted upstream.
- **Only `r n_plague` independent anchored events, across `r length(mapped_years)` mapped seasons,** underlie the entire onset (not-plague → plague) transition coefficient -- see [Data and anchoring]. Grows only as more seasons get hand-digitised into `recent_plague_maps`, not a code change.
- **The 1985-`r first_mapped_year - 1` historic gap is fully unanchored** -- two fallback anchoring rules were tried and reverted under the superseded (a)+(b) rule (`r/c_anchor_plague_state.R`), and the current rule doesn't reattempt them. 2010-2011's blind recovery ([Validation against known history]) is a genuine, partial positive signal, but any specific historic-year read should be treated as unconfirmed.
- **`soil_moisture` and `min_temp` are untested hypotheses** -- plausible signs, not yet checked against real plague-occurrence data the way `rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak` was.
- **`burrow_count`'s `ae_zoneNSW NW Qld SW` term is a known complete-separation artefact** (that zone's state-2 cell has 12 rows, all zero) -- a targeted exclusion (mirroring `"Qld Central"`'s own panel-wide exclusion) is the natural next fix if pursued.
- **`burrow_count.mean`'s `ae_zoneNSW NE Qld SE` and `season:summer_zone_ne` terms are exactly collinear for that one zone**, since `summer_zone_ne` (`r/d_build_hmm_data.R`) is itself defined as `ae_zone == "NSW NE Qld SE"` -- confirmed live via the fitted model's own joint precision matrix (condition number **`r formatC(cond_number_sup, format = "e", digits = 1)`** supervised / **`r formatC(cond_number_unsup, format = "e", digits = 1)`** unsupervised, both effectively singular at double precision), which is what triggers the `"Inversion of precision matrix using 'solve' failed"` warning seen when [Prediction uncertainty]'s `n_post = 500` sampling runs (hmmTMB's own `prec_to_cov()` catches it and falls back to `MASS::ginv()`, so this doesn't halt anything). `season:summer_zone_ne` was kept rather than removed -- it's a deliberately adopted term with a real, independently-confirmed AIC gain (`r/d_fit_plague_hmm.R`), and the collinearity only degrades `n_post`-based CI width for `burrow_count.mean` quantities tied to this one zone (likely understating rather than inflating that uncertainty, since `ginv` assigns near-zero variance along a flat direction rather than blowing up) -- point estimates, Viterbi decoding, and every AIC comparison are unaffected.
- **RESOLVED AT THE SOURCE (2026-09), was "MASKED, not fixed" (2026-09 earlier this same period)** -- the risk map's own most extreme cells (far-west SA coast) were overconfident, traced live (2026-08) to `rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak:ae_zoneSA Vic Mallee`, by far the steepest zone slope in the model under the then-current FIXED (fully independent, no pooling) per-zone interaction spec -- 2.344, vs. 0.25-1.15 for every other zone -- estimated with ZERO anchored or even raw observation data at the covariate range (`rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak > 2`) actually driving those predictions. `r/d_predict_plague_risk.R`'s `mask_zone_extrapolation` guard (still in place, default `TRUE`) fixed the SYMPTOM at the time (masking cells whose zone-interacted covariate value falls outside that zone's own evidence-bearing training range), but not the cause. The transition formula's own zone slope has since moved to a hierarchical (partially-pooled) random slope, `s(ae_zone, by = rain_whiplash_trough_to_peak, bs = "re")` -- Pedersen et al.'s (2019, PeerJ 7:e6876) "Model GS" -- which fixes the cause directly: SA Vic Mallee's own `S1>S2` slope is now **`r round(mallee_slope, 3)`** (pooled estimate plus its own, now-modest, shrunk deviation), squarely inside every other zone's own `r round(min(other_slopes), 2)`-`r round(max(other_slopes), 2)` range, not a standalone outlier any more -- see [Zone-specific deviations]. `mask_zone_extrapolation` is kept regardless, as a general safety net against any future zone-and-covariate-range combination extrapolating past its own training data, not specifically for this case -- and `aez_adj`'s own geometry for `"SA Vic Mallee"` (which still extends past its real training-data footprint, the other half of the original finding) remains a separate, still-open item.
- **`ae_zone` was not added to `trap_count`** -- tried as a random effect, failed on a genuine data-volume ceiling (very thin zone x state cells), not a specification problem.
- **`bait_history` (recent poison-baiting) was tried as an observation-side covariate and parked**, not adopted -- a real AIC gain, but coefficients that don't survive scrutiny given how few confirmed-baited rows exist in the fitted panel yet. Revisit once more accumulate.
- **The full model doesn't yet demonstrably beat its own best single covariate on an externally-benchmarked skill test** -- at the state x calendar-year grain `covariate_summary.qmd`'s whiplash-validation section uses (2026-09, [Full-model onset skill]), the supervised model's own onset AUC (`r round(sup_auc_annual, 3)`) sits below rain whiplash alone (0.717). Not statistically confirmed either way given only `r sup_n_onset_annual` onset examples at that grain, and the model clearly does discriminate real onsets at its own native paddock-season grain (AUC `r round(sup_auc_paddock, 3)`, same section) -- but a genuine, disclosed open question rather than an assumed win from combining more covariates.
- **One-season-ahead forecast horizon is structural**, not a current limitation -- see [Prediction: current risk map].
